blocks.vol: 改正西國立志編刊行ニ就テ
blocks.text: 維新以來刊行ノ圖書十數万種ニ下ラズ。而シテ其ノ發刊部數ノ最モ多キヲ故中村正直先生ノ西國立志編。及ヒ福澤諭吉先生ノ西洋事情。故內田正雄先生ノ輿地誌畧トス。三書共ニ發賣ノ部數各ミ數十万冊ニ上リ。明治ノ三大出版トシテ今尙ホ書林社會ニ傳唱セラル。其ノ聖代ノ文運ヲ裨補セルノ功多キヤ知ルヘシ。特ニ我カ中村先生ノ西國立志編ハ。其ノ譯語ノ精練ニシテ文章ノ謹嚴ナル。句々金玉。一字ト雖モ苟クモセズ。古來譯書中ノ巨擘。原文ニ優ルヿ數等ナリトシテ廣ク學者士流ノ間ニ賞揚セラルヽノミナラズ。事精神ノ修養ト德性ノ涵養トニ繫リ。當代ノ英俊ヲ皷舞シテ其ノ才力ヲ發揮セシメ。化育ノ贊襄。國運ノ隆昌ニ資シタルノ功甚ダ偉ナリ。乃チ豈啻ダ文運ノ進歩ヲ裨益セルノミナランヤ。文章ハ百代ノ大業。誠ニ先生ノ此ノ書ニ於テ之ヲ見ルナリ。然ルニ本書ノ版權ハ固ト數名ノ共有ニ屬シ。發行者中不幸ニシテ既ニ閉業シタルモアリ。爲メニ久シク刊行ヲ中絕シ。今ヤ市上殆ンド一本ヲ殘サズ是レ江湖諸君子ノ切ニ遺憾トセラルヽ所。不肖幸ニシテ曩キニ教ヲ先生ノ門下ニ承ケ。師恩海嶽。追慕ノ情寤寐止ムヿナシ。今先生歿後本書ノ斯ノ如キヲ見テ嘆惜ニ耐エズ。今回其ノ版權ヲ讓受ケテ茲ニ其ノ刊行ヲ繼續スルニ方リ。先生ノ肖像ト自叙傳千字文トヲ卷首ニ揭ケ。用紙ヲ選ミ印刷ヲ鮮明ニシ。且ツ其ノ一般ニ普及センヿヲ計リ。價格ヲ發行實費ニ改正セリ。蓋シ聊カ師恩ノ万一ヲ報復センヿヲ期スルノミ。

blocks.vol: 改正西國立志編刊行ニ就テ
blocks.text: 戊辰四月余去倫敦時弗理蘭德君以此書原本見贈卷首題此三行乃其手書也今模寫付刻俾子孫永莫忘其所自云
notes: （手書の英文）Professor Nakamura / with H. W. Freeland's / Kind Regard.

chu.n: H・W・フリーランド。イギリスの下院議員を務めた人で、中村がロンドンで親しくした
底本には、この識語の前に、手書きの英文「Professor Nakamura / with H. W. Freeland's / Kind Regard.」（中村教授へ、H・W・フリーランドより、敬意をこめて）が写してある

blocks.kakikudashi: 戊辰四月、余倫敦を去る時、弗理蘭德君、此の書の原本を以て贈らる。卷首に此の三行を題するは、乃ち其の手書なり。今模寫して刻に付し、子孫をして永く其の自る所を忘るること莫からしむと云ふ。

blocks.vol: 中村敬宇先生自叙千字文
blocks.text: 天保壬辰。月建丙午。廿六平旦。生于江戶。幼名釧太。祖妣攸命。後改正直。中村爲姓。父母鞠養。哺乳諄誨。猫犬李梅。忠孝仁義。如斯等字。次第認記。非是夙慧。濡染所致。髫齔挾策。論孟學庸。登樹捕蟬。披草求螢。棗栗勸獎。汪濊恩深。每念到此。涕淚霑襟。燈下針黹。霰雪夜嚴。談話故事。內寓良箴。鼓舞誘掖。賴玆妙法。叱咤靡聞。鞭笞奚及。彊圉協洽。入井部塾。惑溺小說。水滸成癖。就桂甫周。竊習蘭籍。師輒覺察。隨加呵責。迨十七齡。寄宿茗黌。侗庵捐館。一齋主盟。官給薪米。書壓棟楹。春誦夏絃。伐木嚶鳴。吐露肝膽。親似弟兄。講究渾噩。互務提醒。旁嗜文章。蘇潮韓海。興意相會。拍案呼快。廬陵歐九。愛其情至。紆徐曲折。磅礴浩氣。亦喜震川。簡古醇厚。尤重餘姚。具三不朽。眼高手低。邈矣鵠的。欲從末由。瞻望憤激。癸丑乙科。濫竽合式。僥倖拔擢。皐比秉鐸。地占爽塏。聖林翠綠。慈闈健康。庭院肅穆。宕陰息軒。薰陶受益。門有嘉客。趨迎倒屣。佳時令節。交觴迭酌。好吟杜詩。愈於絲竹。禍福循環。治亂反復。蕃舶競臻。率土驚愕。恬熙已久。賢俊鬱抑。廟議翻覆。僉懷怵惕。藤森呑冤。吉田死獄。烈公幽囚。耕雲窘逐。亥歲秋冬。扈駕京洛。擬聚侯伯。君臣輯睦。豈圖世局。弗可收束。以啓鼎革。皇猷恢廓。象山鉅儒。識量超卓。旅亭訪尋。繼燭更僕。惜哉被刺。斃乎道側。踵吾蒙譏。殆罹災厄。攘夷喧騰。扼腕怒目。或緣衷赤。多出計畧。乃倡開港。明白磊落。曷怪衆怨。輻輳攅簇。萱堂見背。將軍薨逝。垢面蓬髮。憂愁隱蔽。忽思壯遊。馳觀域外。吸噓沆瀣。蠲滌濁穢。慶應二載。凌跨大洋。遂抵龍動。術藝之塲。伴侶秀邁。麒麟鳳凰。蒹葭倚玉。鬢毛帶霜。朝課暮繹。較短角長。錐股懸梁。何暇憶鄕。初謂島微。眇蕞越裳。詎料規模。宏濶盛昌。虔奉眞神。振整紀綱。德善慫恿。姦惡隄防。鰥寡孤獨。盲啞癲狂。救恤醫療。條例審詳。厥民活潑。峻偉雄剛。忍耐黽勉。鷙悍奮揚。格物探賾。抉摘祕藏。崇尙實驗。分析毫芒。倍根碩匠。尸祝瓣香。牛董引力。自暗發光。豪傑挺起。斬闢鴻荒。各誇創造。孰甘襲常。樓閣閎麗。崔嵬嶙峋。街市洞達。貨財充塡。綺羅駢闐。車馬殷轔。若夫富強。宇宙誰倫。烏兎迅速。再踰暑寒。桑梓戰作。鴈魚寂然。蒼黃趣裝。過佛郎西。風俗奢侈。金帳寶釵。祗恨期迫。叵暫留稽。美景勝蹟。空付渺迷。歸舟安穩。團欒酒杯。歡極而泣。征途忘疲。回顧既往。領異攬奇。鯨濤鼇浪。屢犯險危。乾坤寧謐。胥仰宸威。遷住靜岡。種菜灌畦。農樵爭席。鷗鳥無猜。芙蓉當牕。著述掩扉。王室維新。方急用材。朋友聯翩。翱翔瑤池。我也東旋。城北擇栖。設同人社。教育英才。遠近來集。謬得虛譽。女子範校。俯瞰茶溪。承乏攝理。誓竭駑駘。幸免罪戾。寔憑僚儕。制度稍備。辟雍轉移。五品叙爵。未報涓埃。嗟爾兒輩。謹聽訓言。勇猛進修。勿憚艱難。寬弘誠敬。恭謙粹溫。懲忿窒慾。止妬克慳。沈湎淫佚。貪樂瞬間。招殃惹咎。貽悔窮年。咀嚼華葩。爛熟典墳。莫沿支流。宜溯淵源。持志須堅。攻業要專。博綜廣採。禁黨戒偏。縹緗萬卷。心血存焉。百家縱橫。經史紛綸。願與汝曹。勤讀終身。

chu.n: 月が丙午に当たること。壬の年の五月は丙午である。中村は天保 3 年 5 月 26 日の生まれ
髫は子どもの垂らした髪、齔は歯の生え変わること。七、八歳のころ。策は書物
十干の丁、十二支の未の古い呼び名。丁未は弘化 4 年（1847 年）で、中村は十六歳
儒者の井部香山の塾
蘭方医の桂川甫周（国興）
茗黌は昌平坂学問所（昌平黌）。お茶の水（茗渓）にあったことから言う
佐藤一斎。前の句の侗庵は古賀侗庵で、弘化 4 年に没した。捐館は死去のこと
『礼記』文王世子篇の言葉。季節に応じて学ぶこと
『詩経』小雅・伐木の「木を伐ること丁丁、鳥鳴くこと嚶嚶」から。鳥が鳴きかわして友を求めるように、友と交わること
渾噩は、揚雄の『法言』が古い経書を「渾渾」「噩噩」と評したことから、古代の経書の奥深い文を言う
宋の蘇軾の文は潮のよう、唐の韓愈の文は海のようだ、という評（韓海蘇潮）
宋の欧陽脩。廬陵の人で、一族の同じ世代の九番目だった
明の帰有光。震川は号
明の王守仁（陽明）。浙江の余姚の人。三不朽は『春秋左氏伝』襄公二十四年の言葉で、徳を立て、功を立て、言を立てること
『論語』子罕篇で、顔淵が孔子について言う「之に従はんと欲すと雖も、由末きのみ」から
嘉永 6 年（1853 年）、幕府の学問吟味に乙科で及第した。濫竽は、力のない者がまぎれこんで席をふさぐこと（『韓非子』内儲説上）
皐比は虎の皮で、師の座る席。秉鐸は、鈴を持つ意から、教官となること。中村は昌平黌の教授方、のち御儒者となった
塩谷宕陰と安井息軒。ともに昌平黌の儒官
客を喜んで、履物をさかさまにはいて急いで出迎えること。後漢の蔡邕が王粲を迎えた故事
藤森弘庵（天山）。安政の大獄で江戸を追われた。次の吉田は吉田松陰、烈公は水戸の徳川斉昭
文久 3 年（癸亥、1863 年）。この年の暮れ、十四代将軍家茂が二度めの上洛の途につき、中村も従った
鼎革は王朝が改まること。ここは幕府が倒れて王政に復したこと
佐久間象山。元治元年（1864 年）七月、京都で暗殺された
更僕は『礼記』儒行篇の言葉で、取り次ぎの者が疲れて交代するほど話が長く続くこと
萱堂は母。見背は親に先立たれること。將軍は家茂で、慶応 2 年（1866 年）七月に大坂城で没した
龍動はロンドン。中村は、幕府がイギリスに送った留学生の取締として渡った
『世説新語』容止篇の「蒹葭、玉樹に倚る」から。つまらない者がすぐれた人のそばにいること。中村は三十五歳で、一行の年長だった
戦国の蘇秦は股に錐を刺し、漢の孫敬は髪を梁につないで、眠気を払って学んだという故事
中国の南のはてにあったという古代の小国
フランシス・ベーコン。底本の振り仮名は「ベイコン」。次の牛董はニュートン
尸祝は神を祭ること、瓣香は香をたいて敬うこと。師として深くあがめる意
烏は日、兎は月。月日の早く過ぎること
桑梓は故郷。慶応 4 年（1868 年）の戊辰の戦い。鴈魚は手紙
徳川家が静岡に移されたのに従い、静岡学問所の教授となった。『西国立志編』はここで訳された
『荘子』寓言篇の話から。気取りがなくなって、土地の人が遠慮しなくなること。次の「鷗鳥無猜」は『列子』黄帝篇の、たくらみのない人にはかもめが寄って来るという話から
富士山
瑤池は仙人の住む所の池。朝廷に仕えて高い地位にのぼること
明治 6 年（1873 年）、東京の小石川に開いた私塾
東京女子師範学校。お茶の水（茶渓）にあった。中村は明治 8 年（1875 年）に摂理（校長）となった
辟雍は古代中国の天子の大学。東京大学の教授となったこと
『易経』損卦の象伝「君子以て忿りを懲らし欲を窒ぐ」から
典墳は三墳五典の略で、古い書物
縹緗は、書物の覆いや袋に使う薄青と浅黄の絹。転じて書物

blocks.kakikudashi: 天保壬辰、月は丙午に建す。廿六の平旦、江戶に生まる。幼名は釧太、祖妣の命ずる攸なり。後に正直と改め、中村を姓と爲す。父母鞠養し、哺乳諄誨す。猫犬李梅、忠孝仁義、斯くの如き等の字、次第に認記す。是れ夙慧に非ず、濡染の致す所なり。髫齔にして策を挾む、論孟學庸。樹に登りて蟬を捕へ、草を披きて螢を求む。棗栗もて勸獎す、汪濊として恩深し。念ひ此に到る每に、涕淚襟を霑す。燈下の針黹、霰雪夜嚴し。故事を談話し、內に良箴を寓す。鼓舞誘掖、玆の妙法に賴る。叱咤聞くこと靡し、鞭笞奚ぞ及ばん。彊圉協洽、井部の塾に入る。小說に惑溺し、水滸癖を成す。桂甫周に就きて、竊かに蘭籍を習ふ。師輒ち覺察し、隨ひて呵責を加ふ。十七齡に迨びて、茗黌に寄宿す。侗庵館を捐て、一齋盟を主る。官、薪米を給し、書は棟楹を壓す。春誦夏絃、伐木嚶鳴す。肝膽を吐露し、親しきこと弟兄に似たり。渾噩を講究し、互ひに提醒に務む。旁ら文章を嗜む、蘇潮韓海。興、意と相會すれば、案を拍ちて快を呼ぶ。廬陵の歐九、其の情の至れるを愛す。紆徐曲折、磅礴たる浩氣。亦震川を喜ぶ、簡古醇厚。尤も餘姚を重んず、三不朽を具ふ。眼高く手低し、邈かなり鵠的。從はんと欲するも由末し、瞻望して憤激す。癸丑の乙科、濫竽式に合ふ。僥倖にして拔擢せられ、皐比に鐸を秉る。地は爽塏を占め、聖林翠綠なり。慈闈健康にして、庭院肅穆たり。宕陰・息軒、薰陶益を受く。門に嘉客有れば、趨り迎へて屣を倒にす。佳時令節、觴を交へ迭ひに酌む。好んで杜詩を吟ず、絲竹に愈れり。禍福循環し、治亂反復す。蕃舶競ひ臻り、率土驚愕す。恬熙已に久しく、賢俊鬱抑す。廟議翻覆し、僉怵惕を懷く。藤森冤を呑み、吉田獄に死す。烈公幽囚せられ、耕雲窘逐せらる。亥の歲の秋冬、駕に京洛に扈す。侯伯を聚めて、君臣輯睦せんことを擬す。豈圖らんや世局、收束す可からず。以て鼎革を啓き、皇猷恢廓す。象山は鉅儒、識量超卓なり。旅亭に訪尋し、燭を繼ぎ僕を更ふ。惜しい哉刺されて、道の側に斃る。踵いで吾も譏を蒙り、殆ど災厄に罹らんとす。攘夷喧騰し、腕を扼し目を怒らす。或は衷赤に緣るも、多くは計畧に出づ。乃ち開港を倡ふ、明白磊落。曷ぞ怪しまん衆怨の、輻輳攅簇するを。萱堂に背かれ、將軍薨逝す。垢面蓬髮、憂愁隱蔽す。忽ち壯遊を思ひ、域外に馳觀せんとす。沆瀣を吸噓して、濁穢を蠲滌せん。慶應二載、大洋を凌跨す。遂に龍動に抵る、術藝の塲。伴侶は秀邁、麒麟鳳凰。蒹葭玉に倚り、鬢毛霜を帶ぶ。朝に課し暮に繹ね、短を較べ長を角す。股に錐し梁に懸く、何ぞ鄕を憶ふに暇あらん。初め謂へらく島微にして、眇蕞たること越裳のごとしと。詎ぞ料らん規模の、宏濶盛昌なるを。虔んで眞神を奉じ、紀綱を振整す。德善は慫恿し、姦惡は隄防す。鰥寡孤獨、盲啞癲狂、救恤醫療、條例審詳なり。厥の民活潑にして、峻偉雄剛。忍耐黽勉、鷙悍奮揚す。格物賾を探り、祕藏を抉摘す。實驗を崇尙し、毫芒を分析す。倍根は碩匠、尸祝して香を瓣す。牛董の引力、暗より光を發す。豪傑挺起して、鴻荒を斬闢す。各創造を誇る、孰か常を襲ふに甘んぜん。樓閣閎麗にして、崔嵬嶙峋たり。街市洞達し、貨財充塡す。綺羅駢闐し、車馬殷轔たり。夫の富强の若きは、宇宙誰か倫せん。烏兎迅速、再び暑寒を踰ゆ。桑梓戰作り、鴈魚寂然たり。蒼黃として裝を趣し、佛郎西を過ぐ。風俗奢侈、金帳寶釵。祗恨むらくは期迫りて、暫くも留稽す叵きを。美景勝蹟、空しく渺迷に付す。歸舟安穩、團欒の酒杯。歡極まりて泣き、征途疲れを忘る。既往を回顧すれば、異を領し奇を攬る。鯨濤鼇浪、屢險危を犯す。乾坤寧謐にして、胥宸威を仰ぐ。靜岡に遷り住み、菜を種ゑ畦に灌ぐ。農樵席を爭ひ、鷗鳥猜ふこと無し。芙蓉牕に當り、著述して扉を掩ふ。王室維新、方に材を用ふるに急なり。朋友聯翩として、瑤池に翺翔す。我も也東に旋り、城北に栖を擇ぶ。同人社を設け、英才を教育す。遠近來り集ひ、謬りて虛譽を得たり。女子範校、茶溪を俯瞰す。乏しきを承けて攝理し、誓ひて駑駘を竭す。幸ひに罪戾を免るるは、寔に僚儕に憑る。制度稍備はり、辟雍に轉移す。五品爵に叙せらるるも、未だ涓埃を報いず。嗟爾兒輩、謹んで訓言を聽け。勇猛に進修し、艱難を憚ること勿れ。寬弘誠敬、恭謙粹溫。忿を懲らし慾を窒ぎ、妬を止め慳に克て。沈湎淫佚は、樂を瞬間に貪り、殃を招き咎を惹きて、悔を窮年に貽す。華葩を咀嚼し、典墳に爛熟せよ。支流に沿ふこと莫れ、宜しく淵源に溯るべし。志を持すること須く堅かるべし、業を攻むること專なるを要す。博く綜べ廣く採り、黨を禁じ偏を戒めよ。縹緗萬卷、心血存す。百家縱橫、經史紛綸。願はくは汝曹と、勤め讀みて身を終へん。

blocks.vol: 序
blocks.text: 歷觀古今來立一事業之人。皆抱百折不回之概。把持牢。立志確。勇往直前。一切不問世間毀譽褒貶。亦且不以一敗。挫其銳氣。然後所期望之事始成。是豈尋常發憤所能屆耶。故凡百術藝。以至人之爲聖爲賢。其成否全存于本身。更不干別人事。所謂豪傑之士雖無文王猶興者。乃是也。頃者。友人中邨敬宇出所譯述自助論。屬予序。受而讀之。編中歷擧西國辛苦立一事業之俊傑。予抵掌曰彼邦亦有此說乎。至裒之成書則妙。士大夫立身骨子。實在此處。此處捉住不失。後來所植立。必有卓然可見者。自助之爲言。殊與子輿氏不動心之旨合。鼓舞年少人。孰如此。敬宇著眼極好。予老矣。莫能爲。所望尤在後生也。感慨之餘。遂題簡端。庚午秋仲下浣

chu.a: 所謂豪傑之士雖無文王猶興者
chu.n: 『孟子』尽心上篇「文王を待ちて後に興る者は凡民なり。夫の豪傑の士の若きは、文王無しと雖も猶ほ興る」
中村正直。敬宇は号
『孟子』公孫丑上篇「我四十にして心を動かさず」。この句の上の「子輿氏」は孟子のことで、子輿は孟子の字
庚午は明治 3 年（1870 年）。秋仲は八月、下浣は下旬

blocks.kakikudashi: 古今來一事業を立つるの人を歷觀するに、皆百折不回の概を抱き、把持牢く、志を立つること確く、勇往直前、一切世間の毀譽褒貶を問はず。亦且つ一敗を以て、其の銳氣を挫かず。然る後期望する所の事始めて成る。是れ豈に尋常の發憤の能く屆る所ならんや。故に凡百の術藝より、以て人の聖と爲り賢と爲るに至るまで、其の成否は全く本身に存す。更に別人の事に干らず。所謂豪傑の士は文王無しと雖も猶ほ興る者、乃ち是なり。頃者、友人中邨敬宇、譯述する所の自助論を出して、予に序を屬す。受けて之を讀むに、編中西國の辛苦して一事業を立つるの俊傑を歷擧す。予掌を抵ちて曰く、彼の邦も亦此の說有るかと。之を裒めて書を成すに至りては則ち妙なり。士大夫身を立つるの骨子は、實に此の處に在り。此の處捉へ住めて失はずんば、後來植立する所、必ず卓然として見る可き者有らん。自助の言爲る、殊に子輿氏の不動心の旨と合す。年少の人を鼓舞するは、孰か此に如かん。敬宇の著眼極めて好し。予老いたり、爲すこと能ふ莫し。望む所は尤も後生に在るなり。感慨の餘、遂に簡端に題す。庚午秋仲下浣。

blocks.vol: 自助論第一編序
blocks.text: 余譯是書。客有過而問者。曰。子何不譯兵書。余曰。子謂兵强則國賴以治安乎。且謂西國之强。由于兵乎。是大不然。夫西國之强。由于人民篤信天道。由于人民有自主之權。由于政寬法公。拿破崙論戰曰。德行之力。十倍于身體之力。斯邁爾斯曰。國之强弱。關于人民之品行。又曰。眞實良善。爲品行之本。蓋國者。人衆相合之稱。故人々品行正。則風俗美。風俗美。則一國協和。合成一體。强何足言。若國人品行未正。風俗未美。而徒汲々乎兵事之是講。其不陷而爲好鬪嗜殺之俗者幾希。尙何治安之可望哉。且由天理而論。則欲强之一念。大悖於正矣。何者。强者對弱之稱也。天生斯民。欲人々同受安樂。同修道德。同崇知識。同勉藝業。豈欲此强而彼弱。此優而彼劣哉。故地球萬國當以學問文藝相交。利用厚生之道。互相資益。彼此安康。共受福祉。如此則何有乎較强弱競優劣哉。夫人知天命之可畏。以眞實之心。行良善之事。一人如此。一家如此。一國如此。天下如此。愛日仁風。四海合驩。慈雲和氣。六合呈祥。如此則亦何有乎甲兵銃砲之用哉。古不云乎。兵者凶器。戰者危事也。仁者無敵。善戰者服上刑。一人之命。重於全地球。匹夫之善行。有關係於邦國天下者。乃以貪土地之故。使至貴至重之人命。橫罹極慘極毒之禍。其違皇天之意。負造化之恩。罪不可逭矣。西國近時大省刑罰。然猶未能全戢干戈。豈其敎化有未洽者耶。抑宇宙泰運之期未至耶。嗚呼。六合之際。禮敎盛而兵刑廢。當有日也。恨余與子未及見之也已。客唯唯而退。遂書以弁卷首。歲次上章敦牂孟夏上浣。

chu.n: 原書の第十三編に「ナポレオンは、精神の力は肉体の力に対して十対一であると言った」とある
『書経』大禹謨の「徳を正し、用を利し、生を厚くす」から。物を役立て、人々の暮らしを豊かにすること
『漢書』晁錯伝などに見える言葉
『孟子』梁恵王上篇
『孟子』離婁上篇

chu.a: 歲次上章敦牂孟夏上浣
chu.n: 上章は十干の庚、敦牂は十二支の午の古い呼び名。庚午は明治 3 年（1870 年）。孟夏は四月、上浣は上旬

blocks.kakikudashi: 余是の書を譯す。客過りて問ふ者有り。曰く、子何ぞ兵書を譯せざるやと。余曰く、子、兵强ければ則ち國賴りて以て治安なりと謂ふか。且つ西國の强は、兵に由ると謂ふか。是れ大いに然らず。夫れ西國の强は、人民の篤く天道を信ずるに由る。人民に自主の權有るに由る。政寬に法公なるに由る。拿破崙戰を論じて曰く、德行の力は、身體の力に十倍すと。斯邁爾斯曰く、國の强弱は、人民の品行に關かると。又曰く、眞實良善は、品行の本爲りと。蓋し國は、人衆相合ふの稱なり。故に人々の品行正しければ、則ち風俗美なり。風俗美なれば、則ち一國協和し、合して一體を成す。强何ぞ言ふに足らん。若し國人の品行未だ正しからず、風俗未だ美ならずして、徒らに汲々乎として兵事を之れ講ぜば、其の陷りて鬪を好み殺を嗜むの俗と爲らざる者幾ど希なり。尙ほ何ぞ治安の望む可きあらんや。且つ天理に由りて論ずれば、則ち强を欲するの一念は、大いに正に悖る。何となれば、强は弱に對するの稱なり。天、斯の民を生ずるや、人々同じく安樂を受け、同じく道德を修め、同じく知識を崇び、同じく藝業を勉めんことを欲す。豈に此は强くして彼は弱く、此は優れて彼は劣らんことを欲せんや。故に地球萬國は、當に學問文藝を以て相交はり、利用厚生の道、互ひに相資益し、彼此安康にして、共に福祉を受くべし。此の如くなれば則ち何ぞ强弱を較べ優劣を競ふこと有らんや。夫れ人、天命の畏る可きを知り、眞實の心を以て、良善の事を行ふ。一人此の如く、一家此の如く、一國此の如く、天下此の如くならば、愛日仁風、四海驩を合せ、慈雲和氣、六合祥を呈せん。此の如くなれば則ち亦何ぞ甲兵銃砲の用有らんや。古に云はずや、兵は凶器、戰は危事なりと。仁者は敵無し。善く戰ふ者は上刑に服す。一人の命は、全地球よりも重し。匹夫の善行も、邦國天下に關係有る者あり。乃ち土地を貪るの故を以て、至貴至重の人命をして、橫に極慘極毒の禍に罹らしむ。其の皇天の意に違ひ、造化の恩に負くこと、罪逭る可からず。西國近時大いに刑罰を省く。然れども猶ほ未だ全く干戈を戢むること能はず。豈に其の敎化未だ洽からざる者有るか。抑宇宙泰運の期未だ至らざるか。嗚呼、六合の際、禮敎盛んにして兵刑廢するは、當に日有るべきなり。恨むらくは余と子と未だ之を見るに及ばざるのみ。客唯唯として退く。遂に書して以て卷首に弁す。歲、上章敦牂に次る、孟夏上浣。

blocks.text: 天地のはしめ潮の沫の凝りて成れる國々多なりけむを荒潮の八鹽路たちへたて遠き境のヿはしも古き御史ともにも志るされすそのくに〳〵の人らまゐ來しとも聞えす大かた唐土天竺わたりを遠きかきりとしそか餘なるをはなへて陸奥の蝦夷の千島のひとしなみになん思へりけらしそも〳〵西洋人の御國に渡りヿは今より三百年餘むかしそ初めなるへきをいくほともなくてとゝめられひとり阿蘭陀の國人のみ肥の國のかたほとりに來りて物易ふるわさをはゆるされにたりされとヿとふ人しも多からすまいてあたし國々の有さまなと聞も傳へさりしをその天の下にありとある國々のヿともかつ〳〵物に志るし傳へられしは新井君美のぬしなん始めなりける其後くさ〳〵の書ともやう〳〵數そひにたれと大かたの世の人は心とむへきものとしも思ひたらすなむあまたのとしをはへにけるかくて近き十年あまりこのかた外國人多くまうてき御國人はたかなたにも往かふ道ひらけしより今いはるけき異國ふりもよろつおほろけならす成きつる物から猶えみしとたにいへはひたふるに大は小をかね强は弱を志のきて獸のくひあふかヿきものとのみおもへる人しもそ多かめるこゝに中村大人のものせられし自助論といへる書を見るに何某の大人のいひけむ今のえみしは古へのえみしにあらすとの言の葉も志るくけに其說すへて和漢のかしこき人々にもおとらすあはれあたし國人にもかはかり誠實なる心のあれは有けるよと打なけかるゝまてめつらしともめつらしきふみとなん有けるいでや此書世に行はれてこを讀みむ人々其道につきておのかしゝ健く雄々しき志をたて事にあたりてたゆますくつほれすなしおほすへき日本魂ふるひおこさむたよりともなりなましかは大人のいたつきむなしからすいみしき世のをしへくさともなりなましおほよそ天地の間に人とあらんかきりたとひ國をへたて境をことにし打見るすかたうち聞く詞はさま〳〵なりともひとしくみな產靈の神の御靈によりて生れつるものにしあれはおのつから直く正しき眞の道は一すちならて有へしやはそを思はてわたくしの心せはくあらぬ小みちに迷ひなんはあちきなきわさなりかしされは掛まくもかしこき天津神の大御こゝろのまに〳〵天の壁立かきり谷蟆のさわたる極み天の下四方の國人睦み親しみ船腹乾さす柁楫干さす渡りまうてきつゝ物多に滿ち足らはせる大御國もいよいよます〳〵榮え行なんものそとおのか心に思ふヿを大人にきこえしかはさらはそのよしいかさまにも書志るして此書のはしに添へよといはるゝかいなみかたくて拙きヿの葉くた〳〵しくかいつけたるになむ時は明治三とせといふとしの長月はかり

blocks.genbun:
THE origin of this book may be briefly told.
Some fifteen years since, the author was requested to deliver an address before the members of some evening classes, which had been formed in a northern town for mutual improvement, under the following circumstances:—
Two or three young men of the humblest rank resolved to meet in the winter evenings, for the purpose of improving themselves by exchanging knowledge with each other. Their first meetings were held in the room of a cottage in which one of the members lived; and, as others shortly joined them, the place soon became inconveniently filled. When summer set in, they adjourned to the cottage garden outside; and the classes were then held in the open air, round a little boarded hut used as a garden-house, in which those who officiated as teachers set the sums, and gave forth the lessons of the evening. When the weather was fine, the youths might be seen, until a late hour, hanging round the door of the hut like a cluster of bees; but sometimes a sudden shower of rain would dash the sums from their slates, and disperse them for the evening unsatisfied.
Winter, with its cold nights, was drawing near, and what were they to do for shelter? Their numbers had by this time so increased, that no room of an ordinary cottage could accommodate them. Though they were for the most part young men earning comparatively small weekly wages, they resolved to incur the risk of hiring a room; and, on making inquiry, they found a large dingy apartment to let, which had been used as a temporary Cholera Hospital. No tenant could be found for the place, which was avoided as if the plague still clung to it. But the mutual improvement youths, nothing daunted, hired the cholera room at so much a week, lit it up, placed a few benches and a deal table in it, and began their winter classes. The place soon presented a busy and cheerful appearance in the evenings. The teaching may have been, as no doubt it was, of a very rude and imperfect sort; but it was done with a will. Those who knew a little taught those who knew less—improving themselves while they improved the others; and, at all events, setting before them a good working example. Thus these youths—and there were also grown men amongst them—proceeded to teach themselves and each other, reading and writing, arithmetic and geography; and even mathematics, chemistry, and some of the modern languages.

blocks.vol: 自助論第一板序　斯邁爾斯自序
blocks.text: 同志ノ少年、大約百人ニ滿シカバ、ソノ志願、益大イニナリ、敎師ヲ招キ、講談ヲ聽ント企ダツル、折シモ、我〔斯邁爾斯〕コノ事ヲ聞ニ與カレリ、同志者中ノ人、我家ニ來リ、我ガ講說ヲ爲テ、彼等ニ與ヘンヿヲ請ヒ、今マデ爲シヿ、コノ後爲ント欲スルヿドモヲ、備サニ述ル、ソノ言辭、極メテ謙遜ナリ、セメテ我ニ叙引ノ小話ニテモ說キ給ヘカシトイフニゾ、我モ彼等ノ自助クル精神アルニ感動セラレ、竊カニ思フニハ、通俗ノ言語ヲ以テ、講說スルヿハ、我ノ所長ニ非ズ、サレド些少ノ言語ニテモ、勤勉ノ意、忠直ノ意、眞實ノ意、ヨリ發シテ、講說ヲ與ベナバ、後來ニ至リ、或ハコレヨリ善菓ヲ結ブヿモ、アルベケレバ、未ダ必シモ裨益ナクハアラズト、因テソノ請ヲ許セリ、我コノ精神ヲ以テ屢自ラ成就シタリシ諸人ノ遺範ヲ講說シ、人各、大小ニ限ラズ、自己ニ賴テ、萬事ヲ做ベキヿヲ語リ聞セ、及ビ後來ノ福祉安寧ヲ望マバ、各自一箇ノ人、タヾ自己ニノミ依賴スベシ詳カニ「コレヲ言ヘバ、自己ノ勤勉ナル、自修ノ力、及ビ自己ノ定ムル規法、及ビ自ラ撿束スル行事ニ依賴スベシ就中ソノ最要ナルモノハ、人タルモノ、各、ソノ職分ヲ盡スニ、正直誠實ナルベシ、コレ實ニ男子品行ノ尊榮ナルモノナリト」、コレ等ノ事ヲ諸人ノ例ヲ引テ、指示シタリキ、
blocks.genbun: About a hundred young men had thus come together, when, growing ambitious, they desired to have lectures delivered to them; and then it was that the author became acquainted with their proceedings. A party of them waited on him, for the purpose of inviting him to deliver an introductory address, or, as they expressed it, “to talk to them a bit;” prefacing the request by a modest statement of what they had done and what they were doing. He could not fail to be touched by the admirable self-helping spirit which they had displayed; and, though entertaining but slight faith in popular lecturing, he felt that a few words of encouragement, honestly and sincerely uttered, might not be without some good effect. And in this spirit he addressed them on more than one occasion, citing examples of what other men had done, as illustrations of what each might, in a greater or less degree, do for himself; and pointing out that their happiness and well-being as individuals in after life, must necessarily depend mainly upon themselves—upon their own diligent self-culture, self-discipline, and self-control—and, above all, on that honest and upright performance of individual duty, which is the glory of manly character.

blocks.text: コノ敎訓ハ、所羅門〔古ヘ以色列ノ賢王ノ名〕ノ箴言、〔バイブルノ中ノプロバルブス、〕ト全ク同ジクシテ、少シモ新ラシキヿナク、又別ニ造リ出シタルモノナシ、我ガ敎誨、舊ニ仍テ過ズト雖𪜈、甚ハダコノ少年ニ悅バレ、接受セラレタリ、サテコノ少年各堅志勉力ヲ以テ、ソノ生涯ノ道路ヲ行キ、大人トナルニ及ビ、各種々ノ方向ニ進ミシカバ、コノ輩多クハ、有用ノ職事ニ任ズル人トナリタリ、コノ敎訓ヲ爲シヨリ以來、數年ヲ經、ソノ事、忘レタルガ如クナリシニ、或夜忽チ一人ノ客、鑄鐵塲ノ工塲ヨリ、新ニ來ルモノト覺シキモノ、訪ヒ來リ、我ニ語ツテ、某ハ今工人ヲ使ヒ、富饒ナル人トナレリ、抑モ昔年、先生懇ゴロニ我輩ヲ敎誨シ玉シヿヲ憶ヒ出シ、感恩ノ情ニ堪ズ、某生涯ノ路ヲ行キ、利運ヲ得タルハ、實ニ先生ノ訓導ノ力ニ賴レリ、先生ノ吾輩ヲ勸勉激勵シ玉ヒシ精神ニ負クマジト、常々志ザシ、遂ニ利達ヲ致シタリト言ルヲ聞シヿノアリニキ、
blocks.genbun: There was nothing in the slightest degree new or original in this counsel, which was as old as the Proverbs of Solomon, and possibly quite as familiar. But old-fashioned though the advice may have been, it was welcomed. The youths went forward in their course; worked on with energy and resolution; and, reaching manhood, they went forth in various directions into the world, where many of them now occupy positions of trust and usefulness. Several years after the incidents referred to, the subject was unexpectedly recalled to the author’s recollection by an evening visit from a young man—apparently fresh from the work of a foundry—who explained that he was now an employer of labour and a thriving man; and he was pleased to remember with gratitude the words spoken in all honesty to him and to his fellow-pupils years before, and even to attribute some measure of his success in life to the endeavours which he had made to work up to their spirit.

blocks.vol: 自助論再版原序
blocks.text: 此書ハ、既ニ英國并ニ他國ニ博ク行ハルヽモノヲ再校スルモノナリ、亞米利加ニ數種ノ板アリテ印行シ、和蘭、法蘭西、日耳曼、領墨ノ人各、ソノ邦語ヲ以テ譯セリ、「コノ書ハ、前人ノ行狀ヲ載タレバ、讀者必ズ前人ノ勞苦ヲ經、試驗ヲ積ミ、難事ニ耐ヘテ、大業ヲ成就スルヲ觀テ、奮發ノ意ヲ生ズベキナリ、
blocks.genbun: THIS is a revised edition of a book which has already been received with considerable favour at home and abroad. It has been reprinted in various forms in America; translations have appeared in Dutch and French, and others are about to appear in German and Danish. The book has, doubtless, proved attractive to readers in different countries by reason of the variety of anecdotal illustrations of life and character which it contains, and the interest which all more or less feel in the labours, the trials, the struggles, and the achievements of others. No one can be better aware than the author, of its fragmentary character, arising from the manner in which it was for the most part originally composed,—having been put together principally from jottings made during many years,—intended as readings for young men, and without any view to publication. The appearance of this edition has furnished an opportunity for pruning the volume of some superfluous matter, and introducing various new illustrations, which will probably be found of general interest.

blocks.text: 此書、既ニセルフヘルプ〔自助〕ト名ケテ、世ニ行タレバ、今マタ改ルヿヲ爲ズ、然𪜈一言ヲ述テ、讀者ノ誤解ヲ防ザルヲ得ズ、何如トナレバ、モシ、人タヾ表題ニ由テ、セルフィシ子ス〔自私スルノ意〕ト混淆シ、自私シスルノ事ヲ讚美スルノ書ナリト思トキハ、作者ノ意ト、正ニ相背反スルヿナリ、「蓋作者主トシテ、少年ノ人ニ、自ラ勤テ當然ノ志業ヲ做シ、勤勞ヲ惜マズ、辛苦ヲ厭ハズ、淡薄ヲ以テ自奉ジ、〔或ハ清廉ノ節ヲ守ルト譯ス〕ツヒニソノ志業ヲ成就シ、自己ノ功勞ニ倚仗シテ、斯世ニ自立シ、偏ニ他人ノ扶助恩顧ニ倚賴スベカラザルヿヲ勸ンガ爲ニ、コノ書ヲ作ルト雖𪜈、然𪜈亦文人、學士、工藝ノ人、新術新器ヲ發明スル人、敎育ヲ掌ル人、仁慈ノ事ヲ行フ人、傳道ノタメニ遠方ニ行旅スル人、傳道ノ爲ニ身ヲ殺シテ仁ヲ爲ス人、此等ノ人ノ遺セル標準典型ニ由テ觀ルトキハ、ソノ自助ルノ職分ヲ盡スノ中ニ、他人ヲ助ルノ意ハ、自ラ包含スルヿ明ナリ、
blocks.genbun: In one respect the title of the book, which it is now too late to alter, has proved unfortunate, as it has led some, who have judged it merely by the title, to suppose that it consists of a eulogy of selfishness: the very opposite of what it really is,—or at least of what the author intended it to be. Although its chief object unquestionably is to stimulate youths to apply themselves diligently to right pursuits,—sparing neither labour, pains, nor self-denial in prosecuting them,—and to rely upon their own efforts in life, rather than depend upon the help or patronage of others, it will also be found, from the examples given of literary and scientific men, artists, inventors, educators, philanthropists, missionaries, and martyrs, that the duty of helping one’s self in the highest sense involves the helping of one’s neighbours.

chu.n: 原文は「いまとなっては変えるには遅すぎる」と言い、この題を「まずいものであった」と言う

原文は「自制」（self-denial）。底本には「或ハ清廉ノ節ヲ守ルト譯ス」という割注がある

chu.a: 傳道ノ爲ニ身ヲ殺シテ仁ヲ爲ス人
chu.n: 原文は「殉教者」。「身を殺して以て仁を成す」は『論語』衛霊公篇の言葉

blocks.vol: 自助論再版原序
blocks.text: 或ハ難ジテ、コノ書、自助ルノ力ニヨリテ益ヲ得タル人ノミヲ多ク擧テ、ソノ敗ヲ取タルモノニ及バズト言モノアリ、コレニ對テ曰、タヾ敗ヲ取タルノミノ事ハ、言ニ足ズ、然𪜈、次ノ書卷ヲ讀トキハ、失敗ノ事ハ、眞正ノ勉强スル人ノ爲ニ、極善ノ敎訓トナルヿヲ知ベシ、蓋シ試爲ノ事、幾回トナク敗ルレバ、ソノ回ゴトニ、益奮發シテ、精力自ラ生ジ、自己ヲ治テ、智識益長ズルヿヲ得ベキナリ、」コレニ由テ觀ルトキハ、失敗ノ事ハ、〔苟モ能ク堅忍耐久ノ心ヲ以テ、コレニ勝タランニハ、〕利益トナリ、敎訓トナル事ナリ、故ニ我カクノ如キ例ヲ多ク擧テ、コノ事ヲ明ニスルヲ務タリ、
blocks.genbun: It has also been objected to the book that too much notice is taken in it of men who have succeeded in life by helping themselves, and too little of the multitude of men who have failed. “Why should not Failure,” it has been asked, “have its Plutarch as well as Success?” There is, indeed, no reason why Failure should not have its Plutarch, except that a record of mere failure would probably be found excessively depressing as well as uninstructive reading. It is, however, shown in the following pages that Failure is the best discipline of the true worker, by stimulating him to renewed efforts, evoking his best powers, and carrying him onward in self-culture, self-control, and growth in knowledge and wisdom. Viewed in this light, Failure, conquered by Perseverance, is always full of interest and instruction, and this we have endeavoured to illustrate by many examples.

chu.a: ソノ敗ヲ取タルモノニ及バズト言モノアリ
chu.n: 原文はこのあとに、「なぜ失敗にも、成功と同じように、そのプルタルコスがあってはいけないのか」という問いと、それへの答えを置く。プルタルコスは『英雄伝』を書いた古代ギリシャの人で、伝記の書き手の代表として言う。中村の訳にはない

chu.a: タヾ敗ヲ取タルノミノ事ハ、言ニ足ズ
chu.n: 原文は「失敗だけの記録は、ひどく気のめいる、ためにならない読み物になるだろう」

chu.a: 〔苟モ能ク堅忍耐久ノ心ヲ以テ、コレニ勝タランニハ、〕
chu.n: 原文の「根気によって打ち勝たれた」に当たる。〔 〕は底本のまま

blocks.vol: 自助論再版原序
blocks.text: 人或ハ功ナクシテ敗ルモノアリ、然モ善事ヲ企テ、成ザルモノハ、善人タルヿヲ失ハズ、故ニ、敗ルト雖𪜈、貴ブベシ、不善ノ事ヲ爲テ、一時或ハ成就スルトモ、タダニ汚名ヲ流スノミ、故ニ人ノ事ヲ爲スハ、善惡何如ト問フヲ要ス、ソノ跡ノ成敗ノミヲ觀ルベカラズ、」然トイヘドモ、善事ヲ志シテ成就シタランハ、失敗シタルニハ遙ニ勝ルベシ、」凡事ノ成就スルハ、人ノ定志アリ、勉力アリ、忍耐アリ、勇氣アルヿノ結菓效驗ナリ、古人曰ク、
blocks.genbun: As for Failure per se, although it may be well to find consolations for it at the close of life, there is reason to doubt whether it is an object that ought to be set before youth at the beginning of it. Indeed, “how not to do it” is of all things the easiest learnt: it needs neither teaching, effort, self-denial, industry, patience, perseverance, nor judgment. Besides, readers do not care to know about the general who lost his battles, the engineer whose engines blew up, the architect who designed only deformities, the painter who never got beyond daubs, the schemer who did not invent his machine, the merchant who could not keep out of the Gazette. It is true, the best of men may fail, in the best of causes. But even these best of men did not try to fail, or regard their failure as meritorious; on the contrary, they tried to succeed, and looked upon failure as misfortune. Failure in any good cause is, however, honourable, whilst success in any bad cause is merely infamous. At the same time success in the good cause is unquestionably better than failure. But it is not the result in any case that is to be regarded so much as the aim and the effort, the patience, the courage, and the endeavour with which desirable and worthy objects are pursued;—

chu.a: 人或ハ功ナクシテ敗ルモノアリ
chu.n: 原文はこの前に、失敗そのものは若者の前に掲げるべき目標ではないこと、読者は負けた将軍や破産した商人の話を知りたがらないことを述べる。中村の訳にはなく、「最良の人が、最良の目的のために失敗することもある」の文から訳している

chu.a: 故ニ人ノ事ヲ爲スハ、善惡何如ト問フヲ要ス、ソノ跡ノ成敗ノミヲ觀ルベカラズ
chu.n: 原文の終わりの文「重んじるべきものは、結果よりもむしろ、目ざすところと努力である」を、中村はここに移して訳している

chu.a: 人ノ定志アリ、勉力アリ、忍耐アリ、勇氣アルヿノ結菓效驗ナリ
chu.n: 原文は、忍耐と勇気と精進こそが重んじるべきものだと言う。中村は「成就は、志と努力と忍耐と勇気の結果である」と改めている
中村が加えた言葉。次の二行は、アディソンの悲劇『カトー』（1713 年）の台詞

blocks.vol: 自助論再版原序
blocks.text: 人ハ、成敗得失ヲ使令シ、己ノ意ニ從シムルノ權ナシ、然ドモ勉强シテ已ザレバ、天賞トシテ、成就ノ賜ヲ受ベシ、
blocks.genbun:
“’Tis not in mortals to command success;
We will do more—deserve it.”

chu.a: 天賞トシテ、成就ノ賜ヲ受ベシ
chu.n: 原文は「成功に値する者となろう」。中村は「努めてやまなければ、天の褒美として成就を授かるだろう」と訳している

blocks.vol: 自助論再版原序
blocks.text: コノ書ヲ作ル主意ハ、約シテコレヲ言ハ、昔ヨリ言傳フル普敎ヲ、少年ノ人ニ申戒セント企タルモノナリ、曰ク、少年ノ時、勞苦セバ、暮年ハ安樂ヲ享ベシ、曰ク、天下ノ事、勤勉學習セズシテ、能成就スルモノハ、決シテコレナシ、曰ク、學者爲シ難キノ事ニ逢ト雖𪜈、ソノ志ヲ折ベカラズ、忍耐恒久ノ心ヲ以テ、コレニ勝ベシ、就中最要ノ敎ニ曰ク、人タルモノハ、ソノ品行ヲ高尙ニスベシ、然ザレバ、才能アリト雖𪜈、觀ルニ足ラズ、世間ノ利運ヲ得ルトモ、貴ブニ足ルヿナシ、我コレ等ノ敎ヲ、世ノ少年ニ曉ント志シ、コノ書ヲ作リ、モシコレニ由テ、發奮勉强ノ人生ジ來ラザレバ、我著書ハ功無シテ敗レタリト云ベキノミ、
blocks.genbun: The object of the book briefly is, to re-inculcate these old-fashioned but wholesome lessons—which perhaps cannot be too often urged,—that youth must work in order to enjoy,—that nothing creditable can be accomplished without application and diligence,—that the student must not be daunted by difficulties, but conquer them by patience and perseverance,—and that, above all, he must seek elevation of character, without which capacity is worthless and worldly success is naught. If the author has not succeeded in illustrating these lessons, he can only say that he has failed in his object.

chu.a: 少年ノ時、勞苦セバ、暮年ハ安樂ヲ享ベシ
chu.n: 原文は「若者は楽しむためには働かなければならない」。中村は「若いときに苦労すれば、晩年は安楽を受ける」と訳している

chu.a: 發奮勉强ノ人生ジ來ラザレバ
chu.n: 原文は「これらの教えを実例で示すことに成功していないなら」

chu.a: 我著書ハ功無シテ敗レタリト云ベキノミ
chu.n: 原書はこのあとに、この版で新しく加えた箇所（低い生まれの名高い外国人、兵卒から昇ったフランスの将軍と元帥、ウィリアム・リーと靴下編み機、ジャカールと織機、パリシー、ベトガー、ビュフォン、キュヴィエ、パレ、フランシスコ・ザビエル、実務家としてのナポレオン、ディールの船頭たち、など）を並べた段落を置き、「ロンドン、1866 年 5 月」の日付で結ぶ。中村の訳にはない

blocks.vol: 自助論再版原序
blocks.text: 論曰、國所以有自主之權者、由于人民有自主之權、人民所以有自主之權者、由于其有自主之志行、今夫三二十家之民相團、則曰村、數村相聯、則曰縣、數縣相會、則曰郡、數郡相合、則曰國、故如曰某村風俗純實、則某村人民之言行純實者爲之也、曰某縣多出貨物、則某縣人民之力農勤工者爲之也、曰某郡藝文蔚興、則某郡人民之嗜學講藝者爲之也、曰某國福祚昌盛、則某國人民之志行端良克合天心者爲之也、蓋總稱曰國、分言曰民、始無二致也、試揭輿地圖而觀之、自主之國幾何、半主之國幾何、羈屬之國幾何、如印度古爲自主之國、今則盡統於英矣、安南古爲自主之國、今則半屬於法矣、如南洋中諸國、今莫不爲西國之屬者、人或祗謂西國有英主良輔、故勢威加遠方、殊不知西國之民、勤勉忍耐、有自主之志行、不受暴君汚吏之羈制、故邦國景象、駸々日上、蓋有不期然而然者、且不獨此也、西國之君、大用其智、則其國大亂、小用其智、則其國小亂、載在史冊、歴々可徴、方今西國之君、不得以己意輒出一令、不得以己命輒囚繫一人、財賦之數、由民定之、軍國大事、非民人公許、不得擧行、蓋西國之君、譬則御者也、民人、譬則乘車者也、其當向何方而發、當由何路而進、固乘車者之意也、御者不過從其意施控御之術耳、故君主之權者、非其私有也、闔國民人之權、萃於其身者、是已、唯然、故君主之所令者、國人之所欲行也、君主之所禁者、國人之所不欲行也、君民一體、上下同情、朝野共好、公私無別、國之所以昌盛者、其不由此歟、余尙記童子時、聞淸英交兵、英屢大捷、其國有女王曰維多利亞、則驚曰、眇乎島微、出女豪傑乃爾、堂々滿淸、反無一箇是男兒耶、後讀海國圖志、有曰、英俗貪而悍、尙奢嗜酒、惟技藝靈巧、當時謂爲信然、及前年遊於英都、留二載、徐察其政俗、有以知其不然、今女王不過尋常老婦、含飴弄孫耳、而百姓議會、權最重、諸侯議會、亞之、其被擇於衆、爲民委官者、必學明行修之人也、有敬天愛人之心者也、有克己愼獨之工夫者也、多更世故、長於艱難之人也、而權詐獧薄之徒不與焉、慢神欺心之人不與焉、酒色貨利之徒不與焉、喜功生事之人不與焉、其俗則事　上帝、尊禮拜、尙持經、好賑濟貧病者、國中所設仁善之規法、不遑殫述、姑擧其一、貧家子女所往學之學院、通計三萬餘有所、學徒二百萬人、晝間有職務者所往學之學院、名夜學院者、二千有餘所、學徒八萬人、凡此係民人公同捐銀而設者、官府不與焉、凡百之事、官府之所爲、十居其一、人民之所爲、十居其九、然而其所謂官府者、亦唯爲民人之利便而設之會所耳、如貪權勢擅威刑之事毋有也、抑以通國之廣、人民之多、豈不無姦宄不法之徒乎、然審其大體則稱曰政敎風俗擅美西方可也、而魏氏之書、徒稱其貪悍尙奢嗜酒、是蓋見西國無賴之徒、居東洋者而概言之耳、何其謬哉、余又近讀西國古今儁傑之傳記、觀其皆有自主自立之志、有艱難辛苦之行、原於敬天愛人之誠意、以能立濟世利民之大業、益有以知彼土文敎昌明、名揚四海者、實由于其國人勤勉忍耐之力、而其君主不得而與也、嘗聞、善馬有駕車者、不加鞭策而自能行、不待控御而自能馳、及御者妄引韁繩、多加撻責、而其馬扞格牴牾、頓致不能行、嗚呼、坤輿之内、何國不善、何民不良、由于御者之喜功滋事、而致不遂其性不能存其天良者、蓋亦多哉、

chu.n: ここからは、スマイルズの序の訳ではなく、中村自身の論である。底本の柱には「緒論」とある
外交などの権を他国に握られた、半ば独立の国
アヘン戦争（1840〜42 年）。中村は天保 3 年（1832 年）の生まれ
清の魏源が編んだ世界地理書。あとの「魏氏之書」も同じ
『後漢書』明徳馬皇后紀の言葉。老いて政治にかかわらず、孫を相手に暮らすこと
下院（庶民院）。次の「諸侯議會」は上院（貴族院）。「民委官」には、底本に「メンバーヲフパーリメント」の振り仮名がある
克己は『論語』顔淵篇、慎独は『大学』『中庸』の言葉

chu.a: 貧家子女所往學之學院
chu.n: 底本の振り仮名は「サンデースクール」（日曜学校）。次の「夜學院」の振り仮名は「イーヴニングスクール」
中村は慶応 2 年（1866 年）から明治元年（1868 年）までロンドンに留学した

blocks.kakikudashi: 論に曰く、國の自主の權有る所以の者は、人民に自主の權有るに由る。人民の自主の權有る所以の者は、其の自主の志行有るに由る。今夫れ二三十家の民相團すれば、則ち村と曰ふ。數村相聯すれば、則ち縣と曰ふ。數縣相會すれば、則ち郡と曰ふ。數郡相合すれば、則ち國と曰ふ。故に某村の風俗純實なりと曰ふが如きは、則ち某村の人民の言行純實なる者之を爲すなり。某縣多く貨物を出すと曰ふは、則ち某縣の人民の農に力め工に勤むる者之を爲すなり。某郡藝文蔚興すと曰ふは、則ち某郡の人民の學を嗜み藝を講ずる者之を爲すなり。某國福祚昌盛なりと曰ふは、則ち某國の人民の志行端良にして克く天心に合ふ者之を爲すなり。蓋し總べ稱すれば國と曰ひ、分ち言へば民と曰ふ。始めより二致無きなり。試みに輿地圖を揭げて之を觀よ。自主の國幾何ぞ、半主の國幾何ぞ、羈屬の國幾何ぞ。印度の如きは古自主の國爲り、今は則ち盡く英に統べらる。安南は古自主の國爲り、今は則ち半ば法に屬す。南洋中の諸國の如きは、今西國の屬爲らざる者莫し。人或は祗西國に英主良輔有り、故に勢威遠方に加はると謂ふ。殊に知らず、西國の民、勤勉忍耐にして、自主の志行有り、暴君汚吏の羈制を受けず、故に邦國の景象、駸々として日に上る、蓋し然るを期せずして然る者有るを。且つ獨り此のみならざるなり。西國の君、大いに其の智を用ふれば、則ち其の國大いに亂れ、小しく其の智を用ふれば、則ち其の國小しく亂る。載せて史冊に在り、歴々として徴す可し。方今西國の君は、己の意を以て輒く一令を出すことを得ず、己の命を以て輒く一人を囚繫することを得ず。財賦の數は、民に由りて之を定む。軍國の大事は、民人の公許するに非ざれば、擧行することを得ず。蓋し西國の君は、譬へば則ち御者なり。民人は、譬へば則ち車に乘る者なり。其の當に何の方に向ひて發すべく、當に何の路に由りて進むべきかは、固より車に乘る者の意なり。御者は其の意に從ひて控御の術を施すに過ぎざるのみ。故に君主の權は、其の私有に非ざるなり。闔國民人の權、其の身に萃まる者、是のみ。唯然り、故に君主の令する所の者は、國人の行はんと欲する所なり。君主の禁ずる所の者は、國人の行ふを欲せざる所なり。君民一體、上下情を同じくし、朝野好みを共にし、公私別無し。國の昌盛なる所以の者は、其れ此に由らざらんや。余尙ほ記す、童子の時、淸英兵を交へ、英屢大いに捷ち、其の國に女王有りて維多利亞と曰ふと聞き、則ち驚きて曰く、眇乎たる島微にして、女豪傑を出すこと乃ち爾り。堂々たる滿淸、反つて一箇の是れ男兒なる無きかと。後に海國圖志を讀むに、曰へる有り、英の俗は貪にして悍、奢を尙び酒を嗜む。惟だ技藝靈巧なりと。當時謂ひて信に然りと爲す。前年英都に遊び、留まること二載、徐ろに其の政俗を察するに及びて、以て其の然らざるを知る有り。今の女王は尋常の老婦の、飴を含み孫を弄するに過ぎざるのみ。而して百姓の議會、權最も重く、諸侯の議會、之に亞ぐ。其の衆に擇ばれて、民委官と爲る者は、必ず學明らかに行修まるの人なり。天を敬し人を愛するの心有る者なり。己に克ち獨を愼むの工夫有る者なり。多く世故を更て、艱難に長ずるの人なり。而して權詐獧薄の徒は與らず、神を慢り心を欺くの人は與らず、酒色貨利の徒は與らず、功を喜び事を生ずるの人は與らず。其の俗は則ち上帝に事へ、禮拜を尊び、持經を尙び、好んで貧病の者を賑濟す。國中設くる所の仁善の規法、殫く述ぶるに遑あらず。姑く其の一を擧げん。貧家の子女の往きて學ぶ所の學院、通計三萬餘所有り、學徒二百萬人。晝間職務有る者の往きて學ぶ所の學院、夜學院と名づくる者、二千有餘所、學徒八萬人。凡そ此れ民人公同に銀を捐てて設くる者に係り、官府は與らず。凡百の事、官府の爲す所は、十に其の一に居り、人民の爲す所は、十に其の九に居る。然り而して其の所謂官府なる者も、亦唯民人の利便の爲にして設くるの會所のみ。權勢を貪り威刑を擅にするが如きの事は有ること毋きなり。抑通國の廣き、人民の多きを以て、豈に姦宄不法の徒無からざらんや。然れども其の大體を審かにすれば、則ち稱して政敎風俗、美を西方に擅にすと曰ふも可なり。而るに魏氏の書、徒らに其の貪悍にして奢を尙び酒を嗜むと稱す。是れ蓋し西國無賴の徒の、東洋に居る者を見て、之を概言するのみ。何ぞ其れ謬れるや。余又近ごろ西國古今儁傑の傳記を讀み、其の皆自主自立の志有り、艱難辛苦の行有り、天を敬し人を愛するの誠意に原づき、以て能く世を濟ひ民を利するの大業を立つるを觀て、益以て彼の土の文敎昌明にして、名四海に揚がる者は、實に其の國人勤勉忍耐の力に由りて、其の君主は得て與らざるを知る有り。嘗て聞く、善馬の車に駕する者有り、鞭策を加へずして自ら能く行き、控御を待たずして自ら能く馳す。御者妄りに韁繩を引き、多く撻責を加ふるに及びて、其の馬扞格牴牾し、頓に行くこと能はざるを致すと。嗚呼、坤輿の内、何れの國か善からざらん、何れの民か良からざらん。御者の功を喜び事を滋くするに由りて、其の性を遂げず其の天良を存すること能はざるを致す者、蓋し亦多いかな。

blocks.vol: 第一編　邦國及ビ人民ノ自助ルヿヲ論ズ
blocks.kotobagaki: 一　自助ルノ精神
blocks.text: 天ハ自ラ助ルモノヲ助ト云ル諺ハ、確然經驗シタル格言ナリ、僅ニ一句ノ中ニ、歷ク人事成敗ノ實驗ヲ包藏セリ、自助ト云ヿハ、能自主自立シテ、他人ノ力ニ倚ザルヿナリ、自助ルノ精神ハ、凡ソ人タルモノヽ、才智ノ由テ生ズルトコロノ根原ナリ、推テコレヲ言バ、自助ル、人民多ケレバ、ソノ邦國、必ズ元氣充實シ、精神强盛ナルヿナリ、他人ヨリ助ヲ受テ成就セルモノハ、ソノ後、必ズ衰フルヿアリ、シカルニ、內自助テ爲トコロノ事ハ、必ズ生長シテ禦ベカラザルノ勢アリ、蓋シ我モシ他人ノ爲ニ助ヲ多ク爲ンニハ、必ズソノ人ヲシテ自己勵ミ勉ムルノ心ヲ减ゼシムルヿナリ、是故ニ師傅ノ過嚴ナルモノハ、ソノ子弟ノ自立ノ志ヲ妨ルヿニシテ、政法ノ群下ヲ壓抑スルモノハ、人民ヲシテ扶助ヲ失ヒ勢力ニ乏カラシムルヿナリ、
notes: * Heaven helps those who help themselves.
blocks.genbun: “HEAVEN helps those who help themselves” is a well-tried maxim, embodying in a small compass the results of vast human experience. The spirit of self-help is the root of all genuine growth in the individual; and, exhibited in the lives of many, it constitutes the true source of national vigour and strength. Help from without is often enfeebling in its effects, but help from within invariably invigorates. Whatever is done for men or classes, to a certain extent takes away the stimulus and necessity of doing for themselves; and where men are subjected to over-guidance and over-government, the inevitable tendency is to render them comparatively helpless.

blocks.kotobagaki: 二　人民ハ法度ノ本
blocks.text: 邦國ニテ立ルトコロノ法度、タトヒ美ヲ盡シ善ヲ盡スト雖𪜈、人民ノ爲ニ眞實ノ助トハ成ザルヿナリ、蓋シ人民ヲシテ、ソノ自己ノ爲トコロニ任セ、ソノ志ヲ伸ルヿヲ得セシメ、ソレヲシテ自己ニ勉勵進修セシムレバ、スナハチ人民ノ爲ニ眞實ノ利トナルヿナリ、然ルニ、何ノ世ノ人モ、ヒトヘニ誤テ、己等ノ幸福ヲ受ケ、平安ニ日ヲ度ルヿハ、法度ノアル所以ニ由ルヿ多クシテ、自己ノ所行ニ由ルヿ少シト思ヘリ、且人民ノ開化ニ進ムヿハ、法度ヲ立ルヿニ由テ得ラルヽモノト思フヨリシテ、法度ヲ立ル事ヲ、分外ニ貴メル通俗ノ說トハ成タルナリ、各府縣ヨリ三年或ハ五年ノ中ニ、一二人ヲ薦擧シ、立法院ニ入シメ、國法百萬分ノ一ヲ議立シ或ハ議革スルヿ、縱ヒ十分ニ能ク其職ヲ盡トモ、人民ノ立身制行ノ上ニ於テ、眞實ノ利益トナルヿハ甚少シ、且コレノミナラズ、昔ヨリ今ニ至リ、日ニ益〳〵顯然トシテ證知シタルヿハ、政堂憲署ハ、陰庇ニシテ陽賞ニ非ズ、奸ヲ禁ジ亂ヲ遏ムルノ用多クシテ善ヲ勸メ行ヲ勵スノ用少シ、蓋保護ノ用ノミナリ、人民ノ生命ヲ保護シ、人民自主ノ權ヲ保護シ、人ノ產業ヲ保護スルマデノヿナリ、律法ハ、タトヒ極善ナルモノト雖𪜈、人民ヲシテ、ソノ或ハ心ヲ盡シ、或ハ力ヲ盡シテ得タルトコロノ果實ヲ享用セシメンガ爲ニ、コレヲ安穩ニ保全スルマデノ功用ノミ、律法ハ、タトヒ極嚴ナリト雖𪜈、懶惰ノ人ヲシテ勉强ナラシメ、奢侈ノ人ヲシテ儉節ナラシメ、爛醉ヲ好ムモノヲシテ酒ヲ禁ゼシムルヿ能ハズ、カクノ如キモノハ、特ニ人民各箇ニ、身ヲ修メ、家ヲ治メ、又己私ニ克ント欲スル志、發生スルニ非レバ、改化スルヿ能ハザルナリ、且他ノ風俗ノ美善ナルモノ、ソノ能人民ヲシテ觀感興起セシムルヿハ、律法ノ權力ニ比スレバ、更ニ大ナリ、
wari: 士農工商ヲ統テ人民トイフ〓ノミニアラズ下コレニ傚ヘ
blocks.genbun: Even the best institutions can give a man no active help. Perhaps the most they can do is, to leave him free to develop himself and improve his individual condition. But in all times men have been prone to believe that their happiness and well-being were to be secured by means of institutions rather than by their own conduct. Hence the value of legislation as an agent in human advancement has usually been much over-estimated. To constitute the millionth part of a Legislature, by voting for one or two men once in three or five years, however conscientiously this duty may be performed, can exercise but little active influence upon any man’s life and character. Moreover, it is every day becoming more clearly understood, that the function of Government is negative and restrictive, rather than positive and active; being resolvable principally into protection—protection of life, liberty, and property. Laws, wisely administered, will secure men in the enjoyment of the fruits of their labour, whether of mind or body, at a comparatively small personal sacrifice; but no laws, however stringent, can make the idle industrious, the thriftless provident, or the drunken sober. Such reforms can only be effected by means of individual action, economy, and self-denial; by better habits, rather than by greater rights.

blocks.vol: 第一編　邦國及ビ人民ノ自助ルヿヲ論ズ
blocks.kotobagaki: 三　國政ハ人民ノ光ノ返照ナリ
blocks.text: 邦國ノ政事ハ、特ニ人民各自一己ノモノヽ、會集シテ放トコロノ回光返照ナリ、蓋シ人民ハ、政事ノ實體ニシテ、政事ハ、人民ノ虛影ナリ、譬バコヽニ一國アリテ、人民ノ品行劣惡ナレバ、一時ソノ政事優美ナリトモ、幾何モナクシテ、ソノ政事必ズ退キ下テ人民同等ノ位ニ至ベシ、又一國アリ、ソノ人民ノ風俗優美ナレバ、一時ソノ政事劣惡ナリトモ、幾何モナクシテ、ソノ政事必ズ進ミ上リ、人民同等ノ位ニ至ベシ、元來邦國ハ、人民ニヨリテ成立タルモノナレバ、人民ノ性行ノ集レルモノ、結果成就シテ、律法トナリ、政事トナルヿナリ、サルカラニ、人民ト、政事トハ、ソノ善惡ノ位價ハ同等ニシテ優劣ナキヿナリ、譬バ水ノ如シ、ソノ升降トモニ、各ソノ自己ノ水平ニ至ルヿヲ求ルナリ、品格尊キ人民ハ、品格尊キ政事ヲ以テ統治セザルヿヲ得ズ、蠢愚ニシテ壞惡ナル人民ハ、自ラ愚ナル政事ヲ以テ管理セラルヽヿナリ、歷ク古今ヲ察シ、成跡ヲ案ズルニ、邦國ノ優劣强弱ハ、ソノ人民ノ品行ニ關係スルヿ多クシテ、ソノ國政ニ關係スルヿ少シ、何ニトナレバ、邦國ハ、特ニ人民各自一箇ノモノヽ、合併セル總名ナレバ、所謂、開化文明ト云モノハ、他ナシ、ソノ國ノ人民男女老少、各自ニ品行ヲ正シ、職業ヲ勉メ、藝事ヲ修メ善スルモノヽ、合集シテ開化文明トナルヿナリ、
blocks.genbun: The Government of a nation itself is usually found to be but the reflex of the individuals composing it. The Government that is ahead of the people will inevitably be dragged down to their level, as the Government that is behind them will in the long run be dragged up. In the order of nature, the collective character of a nation will as surely find its befitting results in its law and government, as water finds its own level. The noble people will be nobly ruled, and the ignorant and corrupt ignobly. Indeed all experience serves to prove that the worth and strength of a State depend far less upon the form of its institutions than upon the character of its men. For the nation is only an aggregate of individual conditions, and civilization itself is but a question of the personal improvement of the men, women, and children of whom society is composed.

blocks.vol: 第一編　邦國及ビ人民ノ自助ルヿヲ論ズ
blocks.kotobagaki: 四　邦國ノ盛衰
blocks.text: 邦國ノ昌盛ハ、人民各自勉强ノ力ト正直ノ行ト總合セルモノナリ、邦國ノ衰退ハ、人民各自懶惰ニシテ自ラ私シ、及ビ穢惡ノ行ノ集合セルモノナリ、是故ニ、邦國ニ於テ最モ大害トナスヘキモノハ、人ノ性行壞惡ナルナリ、此風漸ク長ズレバ、タトヒ律法ヲ以テ一時コレヲ剗除ストモ、再マタ萌發長育スルヿナリ、コレ人々自己ニ過ヲ悔ヒ、行ヲ改ムルニ非レバ、其弊風惡俗ハ、決シテ除キ去ルヿ能ハズ、然ニヨリ、忠愛ニ厚ク、仁惠ヲ好ム人ハ、特ニ法度ヲ變シ政事ヲ修ルヲ事トセズシテ、專ラ務テ民ヲ勸勵化導シ、ソレヲシテ自ラ能ク樹立シ、主張シ、良心ヲ崇シ、善行ヲ修シムルナリ、

ruby.r: スヽメハゲマシミチビ

blocks.genbun: National progress is the sum of individual industry, energy, and uprightness, as national decay is of individual idleness, selfishness, and vice. What we are accustomed to decry as great social evils, will, for the most part, be found to be but the outgrowth of man’s own perverted life; and though we may endeavour to cut them down and extirpate them by means of Law, they will only spring up again with fresh luxuriance in some other form, unless the conditions of personal life and character are radically improved. If this view be correct, then it follows that the highest patriotism and philanthropy consist, not so much in altering laws and modifying institutions, as in helping and stimulating men to elevate and improve themselves by their own free and independent individual action.

blocks.vol: 第一編　邦國及ビ人民ノ自助ルヿヲ論ズ
blocks.text: 凡ソ人、外ヨリ統治セラルヽヿニ由テ生ズルトコロノ利害ハ、ソノ關係スルトコロ甚ダ小ナリ、蓋シ人間萬事、皆ナ人々內自ラ治メ自ラ主ドルヿノ上ニ關係スルモノナリ、是故ニ、君上權ヲ擅ニスル國ノ人民ハ、タトヒ惡政ヲ以テ治メラルヽト雖𪜈、コレヲ稱シテ奴隷ノ最モ卑キ者トイフベカラズ、人民ノ德行ヲ修ムルヲ知ラズ、自ラ私シスルノ心、及ビ邪惡ノ心ニ役使セラルヽモノヲコソ、眞成ノ奴隷ト名クテ、當レリト云ベケレ、カクノ如ク、人民ノ心中ニ私欲生ジ、コレガ爲ニ奴隷トセラルヽモノハ、タトヒ、如何樣ニ法度ヲ變ジ執政ノ人ヲ改ルトモ、コレ等ノ事ノミニテハ、コノ奴隷ヲ救フテ、自主ノ人ニ化セシムルヿ能ハザルナリ、ソノ國ノ政府ニテ、自由ノ權ヲ專ニシ、人民ヲ抑下スルヿヲ以テ善シトスル不祥ノ謬說行ハルヽ間ハ、官吏ヲ換ヘ政事ヲ變ズル等ノ事ヲ爲シ、イカホド力ヲ竭スモ、サラニソノ益アルベカラズ、譬バ玻瓈鏡ニ顯ハルヽ畫影ノ種々ニ變動流移スルガ如ク、ツヒニ著落セル實形トナリテ、永續スル功效ハ、アラザルナリ、邦國ニ自主自立ノ權アルヿナレ𪜈、ソノ自主ノ基礎ハ、人民ノ性行ノ上ニ在ナリ、而シテコノ人民ノ性行ハ、實ニ衆志ヲ合セ、保全ヲ謀リ、邦國百事ヲシテ上進セシムルノ擔保ナリ、
blocks.genbun: It may be of comparatively little consequence how a man is governed from without, whilst everything depends upon how he governs himself from within. The greatest slave is not he who is ruled by a despot, great though that evil be, but he who is the thrall of his own moral ignorance, selfishness, and vice. Nations who are thus enslaved at heart cannot be freed by any mere changes of masters or of institutions; and so long as the fatal delusion prevails, that liberty solely depends upon and consists in government, so long will such changes, no matter at what cost they may be effected, have as little practical and lasting result as the shifting of the figures in a phantasmagoria. The solid foundations of liberty must rest upon individual character; which is also the only sure guarantee for social security and national progress.

blocks.vol: 第一編　邦國及ビ人民ノ自助ルヿヲ論ズ
blocks.text: 彌爾曰、羈政ノ國ト雖𪜈、ソノ人民ニ箇々自立セルモノアル間ハ、極惡ノ徵候ヲ生ゼズ、且何ノ政體ヲ論ゼズ、凡ソ人民ノ自立ヲ壓壞スルモノハ、コレヲ羈政〔又曰虐政〕ト云ベキナリ、
blocks.genbun: John Stuart Mill truly observes that “even despotism does not produce its worst effects so long as individuality exists under it; and whatever crushes individuality is despotism, by whatever name it be called.”

blocks.vol: 第一編　邦國及ビ人民ノ自助ルヿヲ論ズ
blocks.kotobagaki: 五　シーザリスムノ一派ト、自助ノ說ト反對ナルヿヲ論ズ
blocks.text: 人世ヲ治ムル道ヲ論ズルニ、古ヨリ謬說互ニ轉ジテ主トナリ、週シテ復始マルヿナリ、或ハシーザルス〔羅馬古代ノ帝ニシテ國權ヲ己ニ專ニスルモノナレバ、權勢ヲ人君ニ歸セント欲スル政學家ノ名トナレリ、〕ヲ主トシ、或ハ人民ヲ主トシ、或ハ英國君民協議シテ定ムルトコロノ律例ヲ宗トセリ、然レドモ、自立ノ根元ヲ論ゼザレバ、皆迷謬ヲ免カレズ、シーザルスハ、人民ノ己ヲ認テ君主トナシテ順從スルモノハ、コレヲシテ福利ヲ得セシムルヿヲ務ム、コノ敎派ハ、人民ノ爲ニ、百事ヲ具ント欲ス、人民ニ由テ、一事ヲ成ヿヲ欲セズ、コノ敎派ヲ師トセバ、必ズ衆民天賦是非ノ心ヲ强テ、羈政ニ陷入ントスルノ患アリ、シイザリスムハ、極劣ノ神像ナリ、ソノコレヲ拜跪スルモノハ、特ニソノ勢力ヲ怕ルヽノミ、ソノ甚キニ至テハ、特ニソノ財貨ヲ利スルノミ、自助ルノ說ハ、コレニ比スレバ、遙ニ平穩ニシテ弊害ノ生ゼザル敎ナリ、世人コノ說ヲ能理會シタランニハ、シーザリスムハ、廢棄シテ再ビ興ザルベシ、コノ兩說ハ、互ニ相容ザル仇敵ナリ、維多爾。休哥筆ト劔ヲ論ジテ、彼此ヲ殺スニ非レバ此必ズ彼ヲ殺ス、トイヘルハ、轉用シテコノ二說ノ反對スルモノヲ論ズベキナリ、
blocks.genbun: Old fallacies as to human progress are constantly turning up. Some call for Cæsars, others for Nationalities, and others for Acts of Parliament. We are to wait for Cæsars, and when they are found, “happy the people who recognise and follow them.” This doctrine shortly means, everything for the people, nothing by them,—a doctrine which, if taken as a guide, must, by destroying the free conscience of a community, speedily prepare the way for any form of despotism. Cæsarism is human idolatry in its worst form—a worship of mere power, as degrading in its effects as the worship of mere wealth would be. A far healthier doctrine to inculcate among the nations would be that of Self-Help; and so soon as it is thoroughly understood and carried into action, Cæsarism will be no more. The two principles are directly antagonistic; and what Victor Hugo said of the Pen and the Sword alike applies to them, “Ceci tuera cela.” [This will kill that.]

blocks.vol: 第一編　邦國及ビ人民ノ自助ルヿヲ論ズ
blocks.kotobagaki: 六　維廉。大亘自立ノ事ヲ論ズ
blocks.text: 國政ヲ論ズルモノ、或ハ人民ヲ主トシ、或ハ君民協議ノ法ヲ主トス、然ドモ自立ノ根源ヲ論ゼザレバ、皆眞成ノ治道トイフベカラズ、維廉。大亘ハ愛蘭ノ忠愛ノ心深カリシ人ナリ、都伯林〔愛蘭ノ都〕ニオイテ、百工藝業展觀會ヲ開キタルヿアリケルガ、ソノ收場ノ時、言タルコトヲ今コヽニ引ベシ、我イマ眞實ヲ語ルベシ、我毎ニ人ノインデペンデンス〔自主自立〕トイフ語ヲ聞ゴトニ、吾國ト吾人民ノ事ヲ想ヒ出サズトイフヿナシ、夫自主自立ノ源、吾邦ヨリ生ズルモノアリ、又外國人ノ吾國ニ來レルモノヨリ得ルモノアリ、然ドモ、我深ク吾心ニ悟レルハ、インダストリアル。インデペンデンス〔工事ヲ勉强スルヨリシテ生ズル自主自立ノ權ハ、全ク吾等自己ノ力ニ依頼スルヿナリ、〕我思フニ、邦民ノ勉强シテ工藝ヲ爲スニ由テ、今日ノ如キ昌運ニ至リ、光輝ヲ發シタルハ、未曾有ノ事ナルベシ、然トイヘドモ、コヽニ止ルベカラズ、邦人既ニ一層級ヲ進メタレバ、コレヨリシテ、恆久堅忍ヲ以テイヨ〳〵成就ノ功ヲ奏スベキナリ、我思フニ、邦人銳意ニ勉强センニハ、今ヨリ後、久シカラズシテ、邦人盡ク同等ノ安寧ヲ得、同等ノ福祉ヲ享ケ、同等ノ自主自立ノ權ヲ得ベキ地位ニ至リ、又外國ノ人民ト、同等ニカクノ如キ福運ヲ受ベキ時、至リヌベシ、コレ予ノ深ク望ムトコロナリ、

ruby.r: シロシロクシロモノノクラベ
ナガクツヽシミガマン

blocks.genbun: The power of Nationalities and Acts of Parliament is also a prevalent superstition. What William Dargan, one of Ireland’s truest patriots, said at the closing of the first Dublin Industrial Exhibition, may well be quoted now. “To tell the truth,” he said, “I never heard the word independence mentioned that my own country and my own fellow townsmen did not occur to my mind. I have heard a great deal about the independence that we were to get from this, that, and the other place, and of the great expectations we were to have from persons from other countries coming amongst us. Whilst I value as much as any man the great advantages that must result to us from that intercourse, I have always been deeply impressed with the feeling that our industrial independence is dependent upon ourselves. I believe that with simple industry and careful exactness in the utilization of our energies, we never had a fairer chance nor a brighter prospect than the present. We have made a step, but perseverance is the great agent of success; and if we but go on zealously, I believe in my conscience that in a short period we shall arrive at a position of equal comfort, of equal happiness, and of equal independence, with that of any other people.”

blocks.vol: 第一編　邦國及ビ人民ノ自助ルヿヲ論ズ
blocks.kotobagaki: 七　貴賤ニ限ラズ、勉强忍耐ノ人、世ニ功アル事
blocks.text: 凡諸邦國、今日ノ景象ニ至ルモノハ、皆幾世幾代ヲ經テ、諸人或ハ心思ヲ勞シ、或ハ肢體ヲ苦シメテ成就セシモノナリ、忍耐、恆久ノ心ヲ以テ職事ヲ勉强スル人、尊卑貴賤ノ別ナク、〔土地ヲ耕墾スル人、鑛山ヲ搜尋スル人、新器新術ヲ發明スル人、工匠ノ人、品物ヲ製造スル人、詩人、理學者、政學家〕コレ等ノ人、古ヨリ今ニ至ルマデ、次第ニ工夫ヲ積メルモノ、合湊シテ盛大ノ文化ヲ開クルナリ、夫文藝ノ事、百工ノ業、コレヲ勉强學習スル人、常ニ相繼テ絕ザルニ由テ、ソノ始メ混沌タルモノヨリ頭緒ヲ見出シ、秩序ヲ定メタルナリ、故ニ今世ノ人ハ、祖先ノ智識勤勞ニ由テ、學術ノ產業ヲ傳リ受ルモノナレバ、コレヲ補修闡明シテ、後人ニ遺ルベキナリ、

ruby.r: ツクロヒヒラキアキラカニ

blocks.genbun: All nations have been made what they are by the thinking and the working of many generations of men. Patient and persevering labourers in all ranks and conditions of life, cultivators of the soil and explorers of the mine, inventors and discoverers, manufacturers, mechanics and artisans, poets, philosophers, and politicians, all have contributed towards the grand result, one generation building upon another’s labours, and carrying them forward to still higher stages. This constant succession of noble workers—the artisans of civilisation—has served to create order out of chaos in industry, science, and art; and the living race has thus, in the course of nature, become the inheritor of the rich estate provided by the skill and industry of our forefathers, which is placed in our hands to cultivate, and to hand down, not only unimpaired but improved, to our successors.

blocks.vol: 第一編　邦國及ビ人民ノ自助ルヿヲ論ズ
blocks.kotobagaki: 八　英人自助ノ精神アル事
blocks.text: 英國ノ人民ハ、自助ルノ精神アリテ、勢力ヲ奮起シ、百事ヲ勉ムルヿ、昔ヨリ風俗ヲ成シタリ、群衆ノ中ニ崛起シテ、其名ヲ顯ハシ、元來貴顯ナル人ノ上ニ出ルモノ、何レノ世ニモ、常ニアラザルヿナシ、而シテ英國ノ勢力ハ、實ニコレニ由テ生ズルヿナリ、然ドモ、コヽニ亦着眼スベキヿアリ、我邦ノ上進スルヿハ、獨リ有名ノ人ノ功ニアラズ、微賤ノ民、ソノ名モ知ザルホドノモノト雖ドモ、衆力ヲ合セ、邦國ヲ助クルヿ、ソノ利益、又思ハザルベカラズ、史冊ノ上ニ、大合戰ヲ記スルニ、大將ノ名ノミアリテ、歩卒ノ名アラズ、然ドモ、歩卒箇々ニ英雄ノ氣象アリテ、善戰フニ由テ、捷ヲ奏スルヿナリ、且人民ノ生涯モ、又歩卒ノ戰鬪ニ比スベシ、ソノ姓名傳ハラザルモノトイヘドモ、傳記ニ名ヲ留ル大人豪傑ト、共ニ世ノ開化文明ノ上進ヲ助ルヿ、甚ダ多キナリ、至微至賤ノ民ト雖ドモ、ソノ職事ニ勉强シ、平生ノ爲トコロ、正直、忠厚、節廉ニシテ、他人ノ儀表トナレバ、ソノ國ノ治化ヲ裨ルコト、獨リ當世ノミナラズ、後代ニマデモ及ブベシ、何ニトナレバ、一人タリトモ、ソノ行狀貞善ナレバ、自ラ他人ニ傳染シ、ソノ模範ヲ互ニ相師法トシ、後代マデ廣ク行ハルヽヿナレバナリ、
blocks.genbun: The spirit of self-help, as exhibited in the energetic action of individuals, has in all times been a marked feature in the English character, and furnishes the true measure of our power as a nation. Rising above the heads of the mass, there were always to be found a series of individuals distinguished beyond others, who commanded the public homage. But our progress has also been owing to multitudes of smaller and less known men. Though only the generals’ names may be remembered in the history of any great campaign, it has been in a great measure through the individual valour and heroism of the privates that victories have been won. And life, too, is “a soldiers’ battle,”—men in the ranks having in all times been amongst the greatest of workers. Many are the lives of men unwritten, which have nevertheless as powerfully influenced civilisation and progress as the more fortunate Great whose names are recorded in biography. Even the humblest person, who sets before his fellows an example of industry, sobriety, and upright honesty of purpose in life, has a present as well as a future influence upon the well-being of his country; for his life and character pass unconsciously into the lives of others, and propagate good example for all time to come.

blocks.text: 凡ソ、人ノ精力ヲ出シ、職事ヲ務ルヿハ、最モ善キ實事習驗ノ學問ナリ、而シテ又大ニ他人ヲシテ、奮發興起セシムルノ益アルヿナリ、彼ノ大小學校鄕塾ニテ敎ルトコロノモノヽ如キハ、コノ實事習驗ノ學問ニ比スレバ、特ニ入門ノ初步ニ過ザルノミ、我等、毎日ノ閱歷ヨリシテ、得ルトコロノ實益ハ、遙ニ、學校ノ敎ノ上ニ出タリ、サレバ、我家ノ中ニモ、街衢ノ間ニモ、賬櫃ノ後ニモ、店舖ノ中ニモ、織機ノ上ニモ、犁鋤ノ下ニモ、寫字房ノ中ニモ、工場ノ中ニモ、凡ソ大衆熱鬧、事務紛繁ナル處、ミナ親歷實驗ノ學問ノ在トコロニアラズト云ヿナシ、カクノ如ク學問スルヲ、彌列爾名クテ人類ノ敎道トイヘリ、卽日用ノ品行擧動ノ上ニテ、自ラ身ヲ修メ、自ラ己ニ克ヿニ力ヲ用ルナリ、カクノ如ク眞實ニ學トキハ、人々一生ノ間、各ソノ當然ノ職務ヲ盡シ、事務ニ應ズルヿヲ做得ベシ、彼ノ特ニ書冊ヨリ學ビ、文字ヨリ得タルモノトハ、霄壤ノ差ナリ、倍根、曰、尋常書冊上ノ學問ハ、人ヲシテ、コレヲ眞實ノ用ニ供セシムルヿ能ハズ、又學バザレドモ、才智アル人アリ、然ドモ眞實有用ノ學ハ、獨ヲブセルヴエイシヨン〔實事實物ニ就テ熟觀審察スル〕ニヨリテ、贏得セラルヽヿナリ、コノ說、人生實學ノ要領ヲ握ルノミナラズ、又心靈ヲ修養スル道モ、コレニ外ナルヿナシ、故ニ斷ジテ曰、人ノ自ソノ身ヲ成就スルハ、作勞ヨリ得ルヿ、讀書ヨリ多ク、閱歷ヨリ得ルヿ、藝文ヨリ多ク、行事ヨリ得ルヿ、學習ヨリ多ク、人品ヲ觀ルヨリ得ルヿ、言行錄ヨリ多キナリ、

blocks.genbun: Daily experience shows that it is energetic individualism which produces the most powerful effects upon the life and action of others, and really constitutes the best practical education. Schools, academies, and colleges, give but the merest beginnings of culture in comparison with it. Far more influential is the life-education daily given in our homes, in the streets, behind counters, in workshops, at the loom and the plough, in counting-houses and manufactories, and in the busy haunts of men. This is that finishing instruction as members of society, which Schiller designated “the education of the human race,” consisting in action, conduct, self-culture, self-control,—all that tends to discipline a man truly, and fit him for the proper performance of the duties and business of life,—a kind of education not to be learnt from books, or acquired by any amount of mere literary training. With his usual weight of words Bacon observes, that “Studies teach not their own use; but that is a wisdom without them, and above them, won by observation;” a remark that holds true of actual life, as well as of the cultivation of the intellect itself. For all experience serves to illustrate and enforce the lesson, that a man perfects himself by work more than by reading,—that it is life rather than literature, action rather than study, and character rather than biography, which tend perpetually to renovate mankind.

blocks.kotobagaki: 十　言行錄ノ人ニ益アル事
blocks.text: 然ト雖𪜈、豪傑ノ言行錄、就中、善人君子ノ言行錄、最モ他人ヲ輔助シ、倡導シ、勸勵スルヿナレバ、ソノ敎訓トナリ、裨益トナルヿ、甚多シ、ソノ極善ナル人ノ言行ハ、殆ド福音書ニ均シク、ソノ高潔ノ生涯、高潔ノ志念、幷ニソノ己ヲ善シ、又天下ヲ善セント欲シテ爲トコロノ、適徃剛烈ノ行狀、ミナ世ノ敎トナルヿナリ、言行錄ノ中ニ載タル前人ノ模範、〔卽ソノ自助ル力、耐久ノ志、堅忍ノ作業、信實ノ行〕ヲ觀ルトキハ、人々自己ノ體面ヲ存スルノ力、幷ニ自己ニ依頼スルヿノ力ハ、能極卑微ノ人ヲシテ、自ラ該得ノ富貴ヲ造リ出シ、不泯ノ名聲ヲ建立セシムルヿヲ知ベキナリ、
blocks.genbun: Biographies of great, but especially of good men, are nevertheless most instructive and useful, as helps, guides, and incentives to others. Some of the best are almost equivalent to gospels—teaching high living, high thinking, and energetic action for their own and the world’s good. The valuable examples which they furnish of the power of self-help, of patient purpose, resolute working, and steadfast integrity, issuing in the formation of truly noble and manly character, exhibit in language not to be misunderstood, what it is in the power of each to accomplish for himself; and eloquently illustrate the efficacy of self-respect and self-reliance in enabling men of even the humblest rank to work out for themselves an honourable competency and a solid reputation.

blocks.vol: 第一編　邦國及ビ人民ノ自助ルヿヲ論ズ
blocks.kotobagaki: 十一　大人豪傑ハ貴賤貧富ニ拘ラザル事
blocks.text: 學術文藝ノ大家、大志ヲ抱ク傳法敎師、及ビ寛仁大度ノ爵位アル人ハ、固ヨリ定リタル地位ヨリ出ルニアラズ、又限リタル種族ヨリ出ルニアラズ、コレ皆或ハ學校ヨリ、或ハ工塲ヨリ、或ハ農家ヨリ、或ハ貧民ノ陋屋ヨリ、或ハ貴人ノ大館ヨリ出ルヿニシテ、差別アラヌヿナリ、有名ノ傳法敎師トナレルモノニシテ、步卒ヨリ出タルモノアリ、蓋シ貧苦艱難ノ二者ハ、決シテ人ノ進路ヲ妨ルモノニアラズ、何ニトナレバ、極貧ノ人、時トシテハ、極髙ノ地位ヲ占ルヿアリ、又踰越スベカラザルガ如キ艱難アリト雖𪜈、終ニハソノ障礙スルモノ除去テ、必ズ亨通ノ路ヲ得ルナリ、且此ノミナラズ、艱難ノ事ハ、毎ニ人ヲシテ勞苦忍耐ノ力ヲ惹起シ、非常ノ才能ヲ發生セシムルヿナレバ、輔助ノ最モ善者ト稱シテ可ナリ、古ヨリ障礙ヲ踰越シ、奇勳ヲ撻得スルモノ、ソノ例甚多キヲ觀ルトキハ、「人一志ヲ以テ萬事ヲ爲得ベシ」ト云ヘル、諺ノ謬ザルヲ知ニ足リ、ソノ著ルキ例ヲ擧テ、コレヲ證スベシ、上帝道學士ニシテ詩人ナル惹列迷。蓼洛爾、紡糸機器ヲ創造シ、製棉工塲ノ元祖タル、力査。阿克來、司法官ノ有名ナル典的兒田、山水畫工ノ絕技ナル篤爾涅兒、巳上數人ハ、皆始ハ剃頭業ヲ爲セシモノナリ、
blocks.genbun: Great men of science, literature, and art—apostles of great thoughts and lords of the great heart—have belonged to no exclusive class nor rank in life. They have come alike from colleges, workshops, and farmhouses,—from the huts of poor men and the mansions of the rich. Some of God’s greatest apostles have come from “the ranks.” The poorest have sometimes taken the highest places; nor have difficulties apparently the most insuperable proved obstacles in their way. Those very difficulties, in many instances, would ever seem to have been their best helpers, by evoking their powers of labour and endurance, and stimulating into life faculties which might otherwise have lain dormant. The instances of obstacles thus surmounted, and of triumphs thus achieved, are indeed so numerous, as almost to justify the proverb that “with Will one can do anything.” Take, for instance, the remarkable fact, that from the barber’s shop came Jeremy Taylor, the most poetical of divines; Sir Richard Arkwright, the inventor of the spinning-jenny and founder of the cotton manufacture; Lord Tenterden, one of the most distinguished of Lord Chief Justices; and Turner, the greatest among landscape painters.

blocks.vol: 第一編　邦國及ビ人民ノ自助ルヿヲ論ズ
blocks.kotobagaki: 十二　舌克斯畢ノ事
blocks.text: 英國詞曲ノ名家ナル舌克斯畢ハ、元來何ナル種族ヨリ出シヤ、ソノ說種々ニシテ定マラズ、然ドモ、卑賤ヨリ發達シタルコトハ疑ナシ、ソノ父ハ、屠者及ビ牧人ニシテ舌克斯畢幼時獸毛ヲ梳スルヲ業トセリ、或ハ曰ク、舌氏始メ鄕塾ニ在テ助敎タリ、後ニ或人家ノ書辨トナレリ、舌氏ハ、凡ソ所有人類ノ事ヲ知タレバ、人間萬類ノ撮要錄〔人間萬類ノ事ヲ一身ニ藏シタルユヱニカク比較シテイフ〕ト名ルモ可ナリ、ソノ舟人ノ諺語ヲ用フルコト切當ニシテ謬ザルガユヱニ、或ハ舌氏ハ必ズ水手タリシヿアルベシトイヘリ、ソノ著書中ニ、傳法敎師ノ事ヲ委曲ヲ盡シタレバ、舌氏ハ必ズ牧師ノ書班タリシヿアルベシト考論スルモノアリ、又ソノ馬ノ皮肉ヲ能分別定斷シタレバ、或ハ馬商ナリシトモ云ヘリ、
blocks.genbun: No one knows to a certainty what Shakespeare was; but it is unquestionable that he sprang from a humble rank. His father was a butcher and grazier; and Shakespeare himself is supposed to have been in early life a woolcomber; whilst others aver that he was an usher in a school and afterwards a scrivener’s clerk. He truly seems to have been “not one, but all mankind’s epitome.” For such is the accuracy of his sea phrases that a naval writer alleges that he must have been a sailor; whilst a clergyman infers, from internal evidence in his writings, that he was probably a parson’s clerk; and a distinguished judge of horse-flesh insists that he must have been a horse-dealer.

blocks.text: 然ルニ、舌氏ハ切ニ優人ナリシナリ、ソノ年時ヲ送ル間、平生試驗觀察ニ由テ得タル學識ヲ、盡ク戲曲ニ顯ハセリ、蓋シ舌氏ハ深沈ナル書生ニシテ、勉强シテ業ヲ做セル人ナルヿハ疑ナシ、ソノ著ハストコロノ書、人心ヲ感ゼシメ、我英人ノ品行ヲ造リ成スノ益アリ、今日ニ至テ、盛ニ世ニ重ゼラル、
blocks.genbun: Shakespeare was certainly an actor, and in the course of his life “played many parts,” gathering his wonderful stores of knowledge from a wide field of experience and observation. In any event, he must have been a close student and a hard worker; and to this day his writings continue to exercise a powerful influence on the formation of English character.

blocks.kotobagaki: 十三　貧賤ヨリ出タル豪傑ノ人
blocks.text: 日工ヨリシテ起レルモノハ、量地官タル伯倫德例、航海ニ長ゼル古克、詩人溥爾尼斯等ナリ、坊者磚人ヨリ出モノヽ、中ニ、便。戎孫ハ手ニ、鏝ヲ持シ、懷中ニ書ヲ納レテ、操作セシトイヘリ、ソノ他、量地官タル義德瓦圖、及ビ的爾福德、地學博士タル休。彌爾列爾、著書家及ビ雕像匠タル亞蘭。勘邊舎、ミナ坊人磚人ヨリ出タル人ナリ、木匠ヨリ出タル卓犖ノ人ニハ、建造工人タル意尼額。若涅士、時辰標ノ有名ノ工人赫利孫、人物ノ體質ヲ察スル學者潤。翰他、畫家洛模尼、及ビ窩比、東洋ノ學ニ通ズル李、雕像匠タル戎。奇伯孫等ナリ、織工ヨリシテ起レルモノハ、算學家西模孫、雕像工倍根、上帝道學士米爾納兄弟二人、亞坦。話兒客兒、上帝道學士戎。福士的爾、禽學者維爾孫、傳法敎師律賓士敦、詩人丹納喜爾等ナリ、鞋工ヨリシテ起レルモノハ、有名ノ水師提督古勞垤士禮。叔夫爾、電氣博士斯打殘、文章家撒母耳。德留、「クヲートルレイレビユー」〔書名〕ヲ著セル吉福德、詩人伯路模非爾德、傳法敎師維廉。加禮等ナリ、勉强刻苦セル傳法敎師馬禮遜ハ、履法ヲ作ル工人ナリシナリ、近キ數年以來、蘇葛蘭ニ托馬士。義德瓦圖トイヘル草木鳥獸ヲ究ムル深奧ナル學者、マタ鞋匠ヨリ起レリ、ソノ職業ヲ爲ル餘暇ヲ以テ、コノ學科ニ心ヲ盡シケルガ、小蟹ノ類ヲ査究シテ、新ニ一種ヲ看出シタリ、學士家因テコノ蟲ヲ、ブラニザユドワルジアイト名タリ、

blocks.genbun:
The common class of day labourers has given us Brindley the engineer, Cook the navigator, and Burns the poet. Masons and bricklayers can boast of Ben Jonson, who worked at the building of Lincoln’s Inn, with a trowel in his hand and a book in his pocket, Edwards and Telford the engineers, Hugh Miller the geologist, and Allan Cunningham the writer and sculptor; whilst among distinguished carpenters we find the names of Inigo Jones the architect, Harrison the chronometer-maker, John Hunter the physiologist, Romney and Opie the painters, Professor Lee the Orientalist, and John Gibson the sculptor.
From the weaver class have sprung Simson the mathematician, Bacon the sculptor, the two Milners, Adam Walker, John Foster, Wilson the ornithologist, Dr. Livingstone the missionary traveller, and Tannahill the poet. Shoemakers have given us Sir Cloudesley Shovel the great Admiral, Sturgeon the electrician, Samuel Drew the essayist, Gifford the editor of the ‘Quarterly Review,’ Bloomfield the poet, and William Carey the missionary; whilst Morrison, another laborious missionary, was a maker of shoe-lasts. Within the last few years, a profound naturalist has been discovered in the person of a shoemaker at Banff, named Thomas Edwards, who, while maintaining himself by his trade, has devoted his leisure to the study of natural science in all its branches, his researches in connexion with the smaller crustaceæ having been rewarded by the discovery of a new species, to which the name of “Praniza Edwardsii” has been given by naturalists.

blocks.text: 裁縫匠ヨリ、亦卓犖ノ才ヲ顯ハセル人出タリ、史家戎。斯到、畫家若孫、嘗テコノ業ヲナセリ、好古斯吳德ハ、波都〔地名〕ノ戰ニ、功名ヲ顯シ、義德瓦第三ヨリ恩賞トシテ、奈的ノ爵ヲ賜ハリシガ、少年ノ時ハ、倫敦ノ裁縫匠ノ徒弟ナリシナリ、水師提督河伯孫ハ、一千七百二年士班牙未額港ノ戰ニ、水閘ヲ破シ勇將ナリシカ、亦コノ業ヲ爲シナリ、河伯孫少時懷的ノ裁縫匠ノ家ニアリケル時、英國一邦ノ軍艦、コノ島ヨリ出帆スベキ新聞ヲキヽテ、急ニ海岸ニ走リ往キ、ソノ光景ヲ見タリシガ、コノ小童、忽チ大志ヲ生ジ、水軍ノ人ドナラント思ヒ、一小舟ニ跳リ入リ、軍艦ノ處マデ潛徃キ、船將ニ乞テ、義兵トナリタリ、數年ノ後、功名ヲ荷テ、故鄕ニ歸リ、昔シ賤業ヲ爲シ小舍ニ來リテ飲食セシトナリ、
blocks.genbun: Nor have tailors been undistinguished. John Stow, the historian, worked at the trade during some part of his life. Jackson, the painter, made clothes until he reached manhood. The brave Sir John Hawkswood, who so greatly distinguished himself at Poictiers, and was knighted by Edward III. for his valour, was in early life apprenticed to a London tailor. Admiral Hobson, who broke the boom at Vigo in 1702, belonged to the same calling. He was working as a tailor’s apprentice near Bonchurch, in the Isle of Wight, when the news flew through the village that a squadron of men-of-war was sailing off the island. He sprang from the shopboard, and ran down with his comrades to the beach, to gaze upon the glorious sight. The boy was suddenly inflamed with the ambition to be a sailor; and springing into a boat, he rowed off to the squadron, gained the admiral’s ship, and was accepted as a volunteer. Years after, he returned to his native village full of honours, and dined off bacon and eggs in the cottage where he had worked as an apprentice.

blocks.text: 然ドモ、裁縫匠ノ大豪傑ハ、安德留。戎孫ニ如モノナカルベシ、卽當今合衆國ノ大頭領ニシテ卓絕ノ行、心思ノ力アル人ナリ、邑中ニ長老タル時、大會ノ中ニ於テ、立法ノ事ヲ辯論シケルガ、衆中ニ呼ハルモノアリテ、曰ク、彼ハ裁縫匠ヨリ起レリト、戎孫コノ譏刺ノ言ニ答テ曰ク、誰ヤラン相公、予ヲ裁縫匠ナリト云ルヿ、予ニ於テハ、少シモ妨トハ思ハヌヿナリ、何ニトナレバ、余コノ職業ヲ爲ル時、良工ノ名ヲ得タリ、又主顧ノ客ニ約シタル期限ヲ違ヘズシテ、善ソノ衣ヲ製成シタリ、ト言シトナリ、カルヂナル〔法官ノ長〕烏爾西、垤夫、亞堅犀德、客爾古。懷的ハ、皆屠家ノ子ナリ、伴陽ハ、補鍋匠ナリ。淑瑟弗。蘭加斯德ハ、籃匠ナリ、蒸氣機器ヲ創造シ、大名ヲ顯ハセル牛國民、瓦德、士提反孫ハ、ソノ始、牛ハ、打鐵匠、瓦ハ算具ヲ造ル工人、士ハ火器ヲ運用スル人ナリシナリ、說法者翰丁同ハ、煤炭ヲ擔フ人、木版ニ畫ヲ雕ヿヲ始メタル伯維格ハ、煤炭ヲ掘ル者ナリシナリ、獨德士禮ハ、步兵ヨリ、河爾克洛弗的ハ、圉人ヨリ起レリ、航海者拔欣ハ、ソノ始ハ、船檣ノ前ニ供事スル人ナリ、古勞垤士禮。叔夫爾ハ、船房ノ小厮ナリシ、花設爾ハ、軍隊ノ中ニテ、ヲポウ〔笛類〕ヲ吹ク人ナリシ、長托禮ハ、旅行スル雕工ナリシ、壹遠ハ、旅行スル印書匠ナリシ、托馬士。老連士ハ、酒家ノ子ナリシナリ、彌開爾。發拉第ハ、打鐵匠ノ子ニシテ、廿二歳ニ至ルマデ、釘書匠ノ徒弟トナリ、ソノ業ヲ爲セリ、今ハ上等ノ理學者トナリテ、窮理科ノ深奧ニシテ解シガタキモノヲ、明ニ辨析スルヿハ、ソノ師翰弗禮。大未ト雖モ、コレニ及ブヿ能ハズト云ヘリ、

blocks.genbun:
But the greatest tailor of all is unquestionably Andrew Johnson, the present President of the United States—a man of extraordinary force of character and vigour of intellect. In his great speech at Washington, when describing himself as having begun his political career as an alderman, and run through all the branches of the legislature, a voice in the crowd cried, “From a tailor up.” It was characteristic of Johnson to take the intended sarcasm in good part, and even to turn it to account. “Some gentleman says I have been a tailor. That does not disconcert me in the least; for when I was a tailor I had the reputation of being a good one, and making close fits; I was always punctual with my customers, and always did good work.”
Cardinal Wolsey, De Foe, Akenside, and Kirke White were the sons of butchers; Bunyan was a tinker, and Joseph Lancaster a basket-maker. Among the great names identified with the invention of the steam-engine are those of Newcomen, Watt, and Stephenson; the first a blacksmith, the second a maker of mathematical instruments, and the third an engine-fireman. Huntingdon the preacher was originally a coalheaver, and Bewick, the father of wood-engraving, a coalminer. Dodsley was a footman, and Holcroft a groom. Baffin the navigator began his seafaring career as a man before the mast, and Sir Cloudesley Shovel as a cabin-boy. Herschel played the oboe in a military band. Chantrey was a journeyman carver, Etty a journeyman printer, and Sir Thomas Lawrence the son of a tavern-keeper. Michael Faraday, the son of a blacksmith, was in early life apprenticed to a bookbinder, and worked at that trade until he reached his twenty-second year: he now occupies the very first rank as a philosopher, excelling even his master, Sir Humphry Davy, in the art of lucidly expounding the most difficult and abstruse points in natural science.

blocks.text: 天學ヲ以テ名ヲ顯ハセルモノヽ、中ニ、哥白爾尼加士ハ、波蘭ノ麵包ヲ燒者ノ子ナリ、客不列爾ハ、日耳曼酒家ノ子ニシテ、ソノ身ハ、給事シケル小厮タリシナリ、亞連白爾士ハ、冬夜ニ巴理ノセン、ジヨン、ルロンドノ寺院ノ石階ニ棄ラレシ孩兒ナリシヲ、鏤玻璃工ノ婦、拾取テ養ナヒシナリ、牛董ハ、蘭覃ノ小農ノ子ニシテ、拉不禮士ハ、紅弗留爾ノ貧民ノ子ナリ、コレ等ノ卓越ナル人、イヅレモ、幼少ノ時、甚シク患難ニ逢タレドモ、ソノ英才ヲ以テ力學セシニヨリ、普天下ノ財貨ヲ以テモ、買ガタキ程ノ不朽ノ大名ヲ得タリ、貨財ニ富ルモノハ、却テコレガ爲ニ、進修ヲ障礙セラルヽモノナレバ、ソノ害タル、貧賤ヨリ大ナルヿナリ、拉蘭日ハ、天學及ビ算數ニ明ナル人ナリ、ソノ父ハ、條林〔以太利ノ地〕ノ武庫ノ官タリシガ、億シ事中ズシテ、産業ヲ敗リ、極貧ニ至レリ、拉蘭日常ニソノ後來名聲及幸福ヲ得タルヿヲ、少時貧困ナリシ事ニ歸シテ、予ヲシテ、モシ富人ナラシメバ、算學者トナルヿハ得ザリシナラン、ト曰リ、
blocks.genbun: Among those who have given the greatest impulse to the sublime science of astronomy, we find Copernicus, the son of a Polish baker; Kepler, the son of a German public-house keeper, and himself the “garçon de cabaret;” d’Alembert, a foundling picked up one winter’s night on the steps of the church of St. Jean le Rond at Paris, and brought up by the wife of a glazier; and Newton and Laplace, the one the son of a small freeholder near Grantham, the other the son of a poor peasant of Beaumont-en-Auge, near Honfleur. Notwithstanding their comparatively adverse circumstances in early life, these distinguished men achieved a solid and enduring reputation by the exercise of their genius, which all the wealth in the world could not have purchased. The very possession of wealth might indeed have proved an obstacle greater even than the humble means to which they were born. The father of Lagrange, the astronomer and mathematician, held the office of Treasurer of War at Turin; but having ruined himself by speculations, his family were reduced to comparative poverty. To this circumstance Lagrange was in after life accustomed partly to attribute his own fame and happiness. “Had I been rich,” said he, “I should probably not have become a mathematician.”

blocks.vol: 第一編　邦國及ビ人民ノ自助ルヿヲ論ズ
blocks.kotobagaki: 十五　クレヂーメンノ子ヨリ名ヲ顯ハス人
blocks.text: クレヂーメンノ子ヨリ、史冊上ニ名ヲ顯ハセルモノヽ、特ニ著シトス、德勒克、納爾森ハ、海上ニ於テ功名ヲ立ル人ナリ、舊拉斯敦ハ、上帝道博士ナリ、雍ハ、農學ノ書ヲ著ハセル大家ナリ、普禮揮爾ハ、算學ノ名家ナリ、白爾ハ蒸氣船ヲ創造セシ人ナリ、烏連ハ、建屋ノ名工ナリ、禮謗爾圖、維爾孫、維爾啓ハ、イヅレモ、有名ノ畫工ナリ、索見某、堪不白爾ハ、ミナ律學ノ大家ナリ、閼垤孫、托模孫、哥爾德斯密士、格列立地、典涅孫ハ、詩人文士ノ最モ著キモノナリ、勞爾德〔爵名〕哈爾定日、參將義德瓦爾垤士、守備何德孫ミナ印度ノ戰ニ功名ヲ顯ハセル人ナルガ、亦クレヂーメンノ子ナリ、印度ノ英領ハ、實ニ中等種族ノ人ニ賴テ、勝得ラレタルナリ、卽屈來武、瓦爾連。哈斯丁士及其他コレニ繼グ者、ミナ久シク商家舖店ニアリテ、職事ヲ作シモノナリ、
blocks.genbun: The sons of clergymen and ministers of religion generally, have particularly distinguished themselves in our country’s history. Amongst them we find the names of Drake and Nelson, celebrated in naval heroism; of Wollaston, Young, Playfair, and Bell, in science; of Wren, Reynolds, Wilson, and Wilkie, in art; of Thurlow and Campbell, in law; and of Addison, Thomson, Goldsmith, Coleridge, and Tennyson, in literature. Lord Hardinge, Colonel Edwardes, and Major Hodson, so honourably known in Indian warfare, were also the sons of clergymen. Indeed, the empire of England in India was won and held chiefly by men of the middle class—such as Clive, Warren Hastings, and their successors—men for the most part bred in factories and trained to habits of business.

blocks.vol: 第一編　邦國及ビ人民ノ自助ルヿヲ論ズ
blocks.kotobagaki: 十六　アットルチース等ソノ他、卑賤ノ人ノ子ニテ名ヲ顯ス人
blocks.text: アットルチースノ子ヨリ、卓越シテ名ヲ成セルモノハ、以德門。拔爾古、斯彌敦、斯格的、窩圖窩士、索末爾士、哈德維克、段寧等ナリ、以上三人ハ、勞爾德ノ爵ニ上レリ、維廉。伯拉克士敦ハ、賣絲商ノ子ナリ、勞爾德。吉福德ハ、德夫爾ノ雜貨商ノ子ナリ、勞爾德。田曼ハ、醫者ノ子ナリ、拔察司答爾福爾德ハ、釀酒家ノ子ナリ、勞爾德。波爾洛克ハ、鞍匠ノ子ナリ、禮亞德ハ、尼尼微ノ故跡ヲ搜出セル人ナリシガ、倫敦狀師館ノ書辨ノ子ナリ、維廉。亞爾摸斯倫ハ、水力機器、及新製ノ大炮ヲ發明セルモノナルガ、亦嘗テ法律ヲ學ビ、アットルチースノ事ヲ爲リ、彌爾敦ハ、倫敦ノ代寫呈狀者ノ子ナリ、波伯及掃謝ハ、賣麻商ノ子ナリ、學師維爾孫ハ、沛士禮ニ住スル製造工ノ子ナリ、勞爾德。馬高禮ハ、亞弗利加ニ旅スル商人ノ子ナリ、基子ハ、賣藥商ノ子ナリ、翰弗禮。大未ハ、始ハ藥舖家ノ徒弟タリシナリ、大未嘗テ云ク、予ノ今日ノ遭際ハ、予ノ自己ニ造リ成タルモノナリ、コレ虛飾ノ言ニ非ズ、心中ノ實ヲ語ルモノナリ、ト云リ、力查。窩蘊ハ、金石草木鳥獸ノ學ニ明ナル名家ナリシガ、少時ハ、軍艦中給事ノ人ニシテ、中年以後ニ至リテ、始テソノ業ヲ修タリ、十年ノ間、醫科學校ニアリテ、潤。翰他ノ集メタル、宇宙萬物及術藝器物ノ目錄ヲ編著セルニ由テ、ソノ博學ノ基ヲ造シトイヘリ、

blocks.genbun: Among the sons of attorneys we find Edmund Burke, Smeaton the engineer, Scott and Wordsworth, and Lords Somers, Hardwick, and Dunning. Sir William Blackstone was the posthumous son of a silk-mercer. Lord Gifford’s father was a grocer at Dover; Lord Denman’s a physician; judge Talfourd’s a country brewer; and Lord Chief Baron Pollock’s a celebrated saddler at Charing Cross. Layard, the discoverer of the monuments of Nineveh, was an articled clerk in a London solicitor’s office; and Sir William Armstrong, the inventor of hydraulic machinery and of the Armstrong ordnance, was also trained to the law and practised for some time as an attorney. Milton was the son of a London scrivener, and Pope and Southey were the sons of linendrapers. Professor Wilson was the son of a Paisley manufacturer, and Lord Macaulay of an African merchant. Keats was a druggist, and Sir Humphry Davy a country apothecary’s apprentice. Speaking of himself, Davy once said, “What I am I have made myself: I say this without vanity, and in pure simplicity of heart.” Richard Owen, the Newton of Natural History, began life as a midshipman, and did not enter upon the line of scientific research in which he has since become so distinguished, until comparatively late in life. He laid the foundations of his great knowledge while occupied in cataloguing the magnificent museum accumulated by the industry of John Hunter, a work which occupied him at the College of Surgeons during a period of about ten years.

blocks.kotobagaki: 十七　卑賤ヨリ起テ大名ヲ得タル外國人ノ事
blocks.text: 自己ノ勉强ト、才能トニヨリテ、貧賤ヨリ崛起シテ大名ヲ世ニ揚シモノヽ、外國人ニ於テ、ソノ例、又少カラズ、畫家古勞德ハ、麵包ヲ作ル者ノ子ナリ、雕像工奇弗士ハ、麵包ヲ燒モノヽ、子ナリ、畫家留波爾德。羅伯ハ、時辰標匠ノ子ナリ、樂歌ヲ作レル有名ノ海同ハ、車匠ノ子ナリ、始テ影相ヲ金版ニ留ルヿヲ發明セシ達磯爾ハ、戲臺ニ用ル風景ヲ畫ケル者ナリシナリ、羅馬法王ト爲リシ額列鄥禮第七ハ、木匠ノ子ナリ、希臘ノ理學家瑟克斯丟斯ハ、牧人ノ子ナリ、羅馬法王亞獨利安第六ハ、和蘭ノ船ヲ漕グ者ノ子ナリ、亞獨利安童子ノ時ニ、學問スル爲ニ、蠟燭ヲ買フ能ハザルガ故ニ、寺門或ハ街中ノ燈アル處ニ就テ課業ヲ爲リ、カクノ如ク忍耐勉强ナルニ由テ、後來卓絕ノ人トナリタリ、金石學者荷壹ハ、織工ノ子ナリ、器學家荷的弗列ハ、阿連士ノ燒麵者ノ子ナリ、算學者約瑟弗。夫理爾ハ、窩吉士耶ノ裁縫匠ノ子ナリ、建屋工丟蘭德ハ、巴理ノ鞋工ノ子ナリ、金石草木鳥獸學者ナル惹士納爾ハ、時立克ノ皮工ノ子ニシテ、ソノ學業ニ從事スル間、貧苦疾病、及ビソノ他ノ災難ニ遇タレ𪜈、コレガタメニ、ソノ勇氣ヲ失ヒ、進修ヲ怠ルヿナカリキ、古諺ニ曰ク、許多ノ做ベキ事アリテ、コレヲ勉做ント欲スル人ハ、必ズ許多ノ光陰ヲ尋出ベシ、ト惹氏ノ生平ヲ觀ルトキハ、コノ言ノ眞確ナルヿヲ知ベキナリ、法國理學算學ノ名家ナル比爾列拉繆士ハ、必加爾第ノ貧人ノ子ニシテ、童子ノ時、牧羊ヲ業トセシガ、コレヲ爲ヿヲ屑トセズシテ、巴理ニ逃徃キ、許多ノ艱苦ニ耐勝テ後ニ、拿華列ノ學校ニ入リ、奴僕トナルヿヲ得シガ、ソレヨリ幾時モナク、當時有名ノ人トハナリニケリ、

blocks.genbun: Foreign not less than English biography abounds in illustrations of men who have glorified the lot of poverty by their labours and their genius. In Art we find Claude, the son of a pastrycook; Geefs, of a baker; Leopold Robert, of a watchmaker; and Haydn, of a wheelwright; whilst Daguerre was a scene-painter at the Opera. The father of Gregory VII. was a carpenter; of Sextus V., a shepherd; and of Adrian VI., a poor bargeman. When a boy, Adrian, unable to pay for a light by which to study, was accustomed to prepare his lessons by the light of the lamps in the streets and the church porches, exhibiting a degree of patience and industry which were the certain forerunners of his future distinction. Of like humble origin were Hauy, the mineralogist, who was the son of a weaver of Saint-Just; Hautefeuille, the mechanician, of a baker at Orleans; Joseph Fourier, the mathematician, of a tailor at Auxerre; Durand, the architect, of a Paris shoemaker; and Gesner, the naturalist, of a skinner or worker in hides, at Zurich. This last began his career under all the disadvantages attendant on poverty, sickness, and domestic calamity; none of which, however, were sufficient to damp his courage or hinder his progress. His life was indeed an eminent illustration of the truth of the saying, that those who have most to do and are willing to work, will find the most time. Pierre Ramus was another man of like character. He was the son of poor parents in Picardy, and when a boy was employed to tend sheep. But not liking the occupation he ran away to Paris. After encountering much misery, he succeeded in entering the College of Navarre as a servant. The situation, however, opened for him the road to learning, and he shortly became one of the most distinguished men of his time.

blocks.kotobagaki: 十八　製煉家卯格林ノ事
blocks.text: 製煉家卯格林ハ、加爾華德士ノ農民ノ子ナリ、鄕學ニアリテ、學童トナリシ時ニ、衣服襤褸ナリシガ、ソノ聰敏ノ才ヲ顯セリ、ソノ師ノ讀書作文ヲ敎ル者、卯格林ノ勉學ヲ嘉テ、童子努力學習セヨ、他日汝聖會保長ノ如キ衣服ヲ着ルニ至ルベシ、ト云リ、一ノ藥舖主人、コノ學院ニ至リ、コノ童子ノ身體壯强ナルヲ嘆美シ、ソノ己ノ店舖ニ至リ、藥材ヲ秤量センヿヲ勸ケレバ、卯格林コレヲ承允シケリ、然ルニソノ家ニ移ルノ後、學問ヲ爲ノ暇アラザルヲ以テ、遂ニコヽヲ去テ巴理ニ赴キ、藥舖家ニ給事センヿヲ欲シ、コレヲ覓メシガ、尋得ザリケレバ、卯格林大ニ勞憊失望シテ病ヲ發シ、病院ニ入ラレ、命ヲ失フベシト思シ程ナリ、然ルニ幸ニシテ快復シ、後ツヒニ、夫爾克雷ト云ル、有名ノ製煉家ニ知レ、私室ノ書辦トナリシガ、多年ノ後、千八百二十九年ニ、夫爾克雷沒シテ、卯格林コレニ繼テ、製煉學ノ學師トナリタリ、加爾華德士ニ於テ、民委官ヲ選ケル時、卯格林ソノ選擧ニ當リ、ソノ職ヲ盡シテ後、榮名ヲ荷ヒ、昔貧賤ナリシ時、離シトコロノ故鄕ニ歸リシトゾ、
blocks.genbun: The chemist Vauquelin was the son of a peasant of Saint-André-d’Herbetot, in the Calvados. When a boy at school, though poorly clad, he was full of bright intelligence; and the master, who taught him to read and write, when praising him for his diligence, used to say, “Go on, my boy; work, study, Colin, and one day you will go as well dressed as the parish churchwarden!” A country apothecary who visited the school, admired the robust boy’s arms, and offered to take him into his laboratory to pound his drugs, to which Vauquelin assented, in the hope of being able to continue his lessons. But the apothecary would not permit him to spend any part of his time in learning; and on ascertaining this, the youth immediately determined to quit his service. He therefore left Saint-André and took the road for Paris with his havresac on his back. Arrived there, he searched for a place as apothecary’s boy, but could not find one. Worn out by fatigue and destitution, Vauquelin fell ill, and in that state was taken to the hospital, where he thought he should die. But better things were in store for the poor boy. He recovered, and again proceeded in his search of employment, which he at length found with an apothecary. Shortly after, he became known to Fourcroy the eminent chemist, who was so pleased with the youth that he made him his private secretary; and many years after, on the death of that great philosopher, Vauquelin succeeded him as Professor of Chemistry. Finally, in 1829, the electors of the district of Calvados appointed him their representative in the Chamber of Deputies, and he re-entered in triumph the village which he had left so many years before, so poor and so obscure.

blocks.kotobagaki: 十九　法國ニ於テ步卒ヨリ登用セラルヽ人
blocks.text: 法國始ノ變亂以來、軍中ノ卒伍ヨリ貴顯ノ武官ニ陞ルヿ尋常ノ事トナレリ、英國ニ於テ、コレニ比スベキ例アラズ、諺ニ曰ク、「功名ノ路ハ才能ノ人ノ爲ニ開ク」ト、實ニコノ言ノ如ク、若登庸ノ路ノ開タルモノアランニハ、我英人モ、マタ必ズ彼ニ雙ブベキナリ、何西、含白爾土、比斯額魯ハ、皆步卒ヨリシテ、ソノ閲歷ノ路ヲ始タリ、何西ハ、王ノ三軍ノ中ニアリシトキ、常ニ短衣ヲ刺繡シ、コレニ因リテ金錢ヲ得テ、兵書ヲ買タリ、含白爾土ハ、幼年ノ時ニ放逸ナリシガ、十六歲ニ及ンデ、家ヲ出テ、南西ノ商家又立翁士ノ工人ノ家ニ奴隷トナリ、又ハ兎皮ヲ販スル人ニ給事シケルガ、二十二歲ノ時、義兵ノ籍ニ入リ、一年ヲ過ザル中ニ、營將ニ至レリ、古禮倍爾、路費伯爾、蘇晒、維克土爾、蘭納士、瑣爾的、馬士色納、仙○細爾、德亞倫、謨拉的、窩熱羅、白西列士、內、以上ノ將帥、ミナ卒伍ヨリ起リ、然ニ、或ハ、速ニ超拔セラレ、或ハ擧擢セラルヽヿ遲シテ、一樣ナラズ、仙○細爾ハ、多爾ノ皮匠ノ子ニテ、始メ戲子トナリシガ後ニ、輕騎ノ兵籍ニ入リ、一年ノ內ニ、甲比丹ノ職ニ上リ、白爾諾ノ公○維克土爾ハ、一千七百八十一年ニ、銃隊ニ入シガ、法國變亂ノ事、未ダ起ザル以前ニ、ソノ籍ヲ脫セラレタリ、既ニシテ、戰爭起ケレバ再ビ兵籍ニ入リ、數月ノ間ニ、ソノ才略勇氣ニ由テ、アジユタント○メージヨア〔副都統〕及バタリヨン〔一旅五百人〕ノ長トナレリ、謨拉的ハ、百律臥德ノ酒家ノ子ナリ、始メ輕騎隊ニ入リシガ、航髒ニシテ、人ニ服セザルガ故ニ、ソノ職ヲ罷ラレケリ、然ルニ、再ビ兵籍ニ入リ、幾何モナク、參將ニ至レリ、內ハ十八歲ノ時、輕騎兵營ニ入リ、次第ニ位級進ミ、古禮倍爾、忽チ內ノ軍功ヲ看出シ、ゼ○インデフーアラーイゲブル〔疲倦ヲ知ザル人〕ト名テ、コレヲ副將ニ擢タリ、時ニ僅ニ二十五歲トイフ、

blocks.genbun: England has no parallel instances to show, of promotions from the ranks of the army to the highest military offices; which have been so common in France since the first Revolution. “La carrière ouverte aux talents” has there received many striking illustrations, which would doubtless be matched among ourselves were the road to promotion as open. Hoche, Humbert, and Pichegru, began their respective careers as private soldiers. Hoche, while in the King’s army, was accustomed to embroider waistcoats to enable him to earn money wherewith to purchase books on military science. Humbert was a scapegrace when a youth; at sixteen he ran away from home, and was by turns servant to a tradesman at Nancy, a workman at Lyons, and a hawker of rabbit skins. In 1792, he enlisted as a volunteer; and in a year he was general of brigade. Kleber, Lefèvre, Suchet, Victor, Lannes, Soult, Massena, St. Cyr, D’Erlon, Murat, Augereau, Bessières, and Ney, all rose from the ranks. In some cases promotion was rapid, in others it was slow. Saint Cyr, the son of a tanner of Toul, began life as an actor, after which he enlisted in the Chasseurs, and was promoted to a captaincy within a year. Victor, Duc de Belluno, enlisted in the Artillery in 1781: during the events preceding the Revolution he was discharged; but immediately on the outbreak of war he re-enlisted, and in the course of a few months his intrepidity and ability secured his promotion as Adjutant-Major and chief of battalion. Murat, “le beau sabreur,” was the son of a village innkeeper in Perigord, where he looked after the horses. He first enlisted in a regiment of Chasseurs, from which he was dismissed for insubordination: but again enlisting, he shortly rose to the rank of Colonel. Ney enlisted at eighteen in a hussar regiment, and gradually advanced step by step: Kleber soon discovered his merits, surnaming him “The Indefatigable,” and promoted him to be Adjutant-General when only twenty-five.

blocks.text: 以上ノ諸人ハ、カクノ如ク、登進甚速ナリシナリ、然ルニ、瑣爾的ハ、始テ兵籍ニ入シヨリ、六年ヲ經テ、纔ニサアヂヤント〔軍吏〕ト爲レリ、ソノ後、次第ニ登進シ、コロ子ル〔參將〕、ゼ子ラル○ヲフ○ヂヴーイシヨン〔一隊提督〕、マーシヤル〔總兵官〕ニ至リ、瑣爾的曰ク、予軍吏ノ職ヲ得タルヿハ、多少ノ勞苦ヲ積リ、ソノ後得タル他ノ位級ニ比スレバ、尤モ難リシナリ、法國ニ於テ、卒伍ヨリ將領ニ登進スルヿ、今日ニ至ルマデ、相踵リ、商額爾尼ハ、拿破崙第三ノ對手ナル大將ナリ、一千八百十五年ニ、王ノ侍衞兵ノ籍ニ入シトイフ、マアシヤル浦紹ハ、四年ノ間、步兵ヲ爲シ後、一官ヲ得タリ、マアシヤル關同ハ、當今法國軍務ノミニストルナリ、ソノ掌鼓卒ヨリ起リシ故ニ、閉爾西ノ集畫閣ニアルトコロノ畫像ハ、ソノ手ヲ、鼓上ニ置ケリ、コレ關同ノ需ニ應ジテ、カク畫キタルナリ、コレ等ノ例ニ因テ、法國ノ步卒ハ、元帥ノ持ル杖ヲ、衣糧袋ニ帶ベキ望ヲ以テ、戰鬪ニ勇志ヲ奮ヿナリ、
blocks.genbun: On the other hand, Soult was six years from the date of his enlistment before he reached the rank of sergeant. But Soult’s advancement was rapid compared with that of Massena, who served for fourteen years before he was made sergeant; and though he afterwards rose successively, step by step, to the grades of Colonel, General of Division, and Marshal, he declared that the post of sergeant was the step which of all others had cost him the most labour to win. Similar promotions from the ranks, in the French army, have continued down to our own day. Changarnier entered the King’s bodyguard as a private in 1815. Marshal Bugeaud served four years in the ranks, after which he was made an officer. Marshal Randon, the present French Minister of War, began his military career as a drummer boy; and in the portrait of him in the gallery at Versailles, his hand rests upon a drum-head, the picture being thus painted at his own request. Instances such as these inspire French soldiers with enthusiasm for their service, as each private feels that he may possibly carry the baton of a marshal in his knapsack.

blocks.vol: 第一編　邦國及ビ人民ノ自助ルヿヲ論ズ
blocks.kotobagaki: 二十　伯洛沙敦ノ事○以下四章、專心强力ニ由テ、卑賤ヨリ高位顯職ニ至リシ人ヲ擧グ、
blocks.text: 英國幷ニ外國ニ於テ、專心强力、久シテ倦ザルニ由テ、卑賤ノ業ヲ爲ルモノヨリ、高位顯職ニ至リ、國家ヲ裨益スル者甚多シテ、世人ノ耳目ニ珍シカラヌヿニナリタリ、カクノ如ク卓絕ナル人ノ生平ヲ觀ルトキハ、ソノ早年ニ艱難ト戰ヒ、災禍ニ敵スルヿハ、後來ノ亨通利達ノ爲ニハ、必用ニシテ少ベカラザルヿヲ知ベシ、英國百姓議院ニハ、常ニ自己ノ力ニ賴テ發達シタル人、甚多シ、元來職業ニ勉强スル人民ニ由テ、選擧セラレ、議士トナルヿナレバ、然アルベキ道理ナリ、英國人民立法ノ權アルヿノ信證ト爲テ、コノ議院ニ於テ、各部落ヨリ薦擧セル民委官ヲ歡接シ尊敬スルヿナリ、近キ比、約瑟弗○伯洛沙敦ハ、薩爾福德ノ民委官ナリシガ、十時議單ノ事ニ因テ議論セルトキニ、嘗テ自ラ棉磨ノ工塲ニ在テ小僮タリシトキ、勞苦困難ヲ受シヿヲ委曲ニ述テ、予コノ時ヨリシテ、他日モシ運會ヲ得タランニハ、務テコノ情勢ヲ改メ好スベシト志タリキト、ソノ眞情ヲ云ケレバ、惹迷士○額拉含、直ニ座ヨリ起チ、闔院喜色ヲ形セルノ中ニ於テ、次ノ言ヲ出シテ、「伯洛沙敦君ハ、カク卑賤ヨリ起ラレシニヤ、余ハ今日マデ知ザリケリ、ソモソモ新起ノ人ニシテ世襲ノ紳董ト、肩ヲ比ベ、位ヲ同セラルヽヿハ、元來議院ニ在者ヨリハ、榮光遙ニ勝ルヿナリ」トゾ言ケル、

ruby.r: ハウスヲフコムモンス
ジエームス グラハム

blocks.genbun: The instances of men, in this and other countries, who, by dint of persevering application and energy, have raised themselves from the humblest ranks of industry to eminent positions of usefulness and influence in society, are indeed so numerous that they have long ceased to be regarded as exceptional. Looking at some of the more remarkable, it might almost be said that early encounter with difficulty and adverse circumstances was the necessary and indispensable condition of success. The British House of Commons has always contained a considerable number of such self-raised men—fitting representatives of the industrial character of the people; and it is to the credit of our Legislature that they have been welcomed and honoured there. When the late Joseph Brotherton, member for Salford, in the course of the discussion on the Ten Hours Bill, detailed with true pathos the hardships and fatigues to which he had been subjected when working as a factory boy in a cotton mill, and described the resolution which he had then formed, that if ever it was in his power he would endeavour to ameliorate the condition of that class, Sir James Graham rose immediately after him, and declared, amidst the cheers of the House, that he did not before know that Mr. Brotherton’s origin had been so humble, but that it rendered him more proud than he had ever before been of the House of Commons, to think that a person risen from that condition should be able to sit side by side, on equal terms, with the hereditary gentry of the land.

blocks.vol: 第一編　邦國及ビ人民ノ自助ルヿヲ論ズ
blocks.kotobagaki: 二十一　福克斯、林德西ノ事
blocks.text: 福克斯ハ、阿爾譚ノ民委官ナリシガ、昔年ノ事ヲ憶ヒ出シテ、常ノ習ニ、「余ハ諾維古ニ在テ、織匠ノ小僮タリシトキニ云云」ト云リ、ソノ他、今日巴力門議士ニ、カクノ如ク卑賤ナリシ人、尙生存セルモノアリ、林德西ハ、舟ヲ有ル有名ノ人ニシテ、近頃マデ、散垤爾蘭ノ民委官ナリシガ、嘗テ政論對敵ノ黨ヨリ林德西ヲ誹謗シケル時、衞毛士ノ民委官ヲ選ブ人ニ向テ、ソノ生平ノ事ヲ朴實ニ語ケリ、「十四歲ノ時、父母ニ別レ、額拉士哥ヨリ、立拔普爾ニ赴ントテ、蒸氣船ニ入ケルガ、船賃ヲ償ヿ能ザルガ故ニ、ソノ代ニ煤炭ヲ積入ンヿヲ船主ト約シ、コノ勞事ヲ爲タリ、既ニ立拔普爾ニ着シテ後、四十九日間、職業ヲ求メ得ズシテ、辛シテ雨露ヲ凌キ、時日ヲ過セリ、後ニ船中ノ小厮ト爲ヿヲ得タリシガ、ソノ堅固ナル善行ニ由テ、十九歲ノ時、船主トナリタリ、年二十三ニ及ンデ、洋海ノ職ヲ休テ、海濱ニ居住ヲ定ケルガ、其後、ソノ身顯達スルヿ速ナリキ、自ラ曰、「予ハ着實ニ勉强シ、常ニ勞作シテ怠ルヿナク、又人ヨリ施レンヿヲ欲スル事ハ、我コレヲ他人ニ施スベキノ大道理ヲ常ニ目存シタルニ由テ、福運ヲ得タリシナリ」ト云リ、
blocks.genbun: The late Mr. Fox, member for Oldham, was accustomed to introduce his recollections of past times with the words, “when I was working as a weaver boy at Norwich;” and there are other members of parliament, still living, whose origin has been equally humble. Mr. Lindsay, the well-known ship owner, until recently member for Sunderland, once told the simple story of his life to the electors of Weymouth, in answer to an attack made upon him by his political opponents. He had been left an orphan at fourteen, and when he left Glasgow for Liverpool to push his way in the world, not being able to pay the usual fare, the captain of the steamer agreed to take his labour in exchange, and the boy worked his passage by trimming the coals in the coal hole. At Liverpool he remained for seven weeks before he could obtain employment, during which time he lived in sheds and fared hardly; until at last he found shelter on board a West Indiaman. He entered as a boy, and before he was nineteen, by steady good conduct he had risen to the command of a ship. At twenty-three he retired from the sea, and settled on shore, after which his progress was rapid “he had prospered,” he said, “by steady industry, by constant work, and by ever keeping in view the great principle of doing to others as you would be done by.”

blocks.kotobagaki: 二十二　維廉○若克孫ノ事
blocks.text: 維廉○若克孫ハ、當今北達比社ノ民委官ナリ、ソノ遭際甚ダ林德西ニ似タリ、ソノ父ハ、蘭加斯德ノ醫士ニシテ、子十一人ヲ遺シテ死ケルガ、若克孫ハ、ソノ第七子ナリ、ソノ子ノ既ニ長ゼルモノハ、父ノ生存ノ時ニ、敎育ヲ受タリシガ、ソノ幼ナルモノハ、父死シテ後、各ゝ離散シテ、自己ニ衣食ヲ圖ルヿトハナレリ、若克孫コノ時十二歲ニテ、鄕校ニ在ケルガ、コヽニ居ルヿ能ハズシテ、一舟ノ傍ニ於テ、曉六時ヨリ、夜九時ニ至マデ、勞事ヲ爲ケリ、既ニシテ、ソノ主人病ニ臥ケレバ、若克孫ニ命ジテ、ソノ寫字房ニ在テ、事ヲ司シメタリ、コヽニ於テ、頗ル餘暇ヲ得テ、英國博物韻府ノ卷帙浩瀚ナルモノヲ、首ヨリ終ニ至マデ通覽セリ、晝間ニモ讀タレドモ、大抵ハ、夜中ノ業ナリシナリ、其後貿易ノ業ヲ爲ケルガ、ソノ勤勉ニ因テ、贏利ヲ得タリ、今ハ若克孫ノ船帆四方ノ洋海ニ駛セ、地球上ノ萬國ト、互市ヲ通ゼリ、

ruby.r: ノースダービイシヤー
エンサイクロペヂアブリタニカ

blocks.genbun: The career of Mr. William Jackson, of Birkenhead, the present member for North Derbyshire, bears considerable resemblance to that of Mr. Lindsay. His father, a surgeon at Lancaster, died, leaving a family of eleven children, of whom William Jackson was the seventh son. The elder boys had been well educated while the father lived, but at his death the younger members had to shift for themselves. William, when under twelve years old, was taken from school, and put to hard work at a ship’s side from six in the morning till nine at night. His master falling ill, the boy was taken into the counting-house, where he had more leisure. This gave him an opportunity of reading, and having obtained access to a set of the ‘Encyclopædia Britannica,’ he read the volumes through from A to Z, partly by day, but chiefly at night. He afterwards put himself to a trade, was diligent, and succeeded in it. Now he has ships sailing on almost every sea, and holds commercial relations with nearly every country on the globe.

blocks.text: 力查○格伯田マタ卑賤ヨリ起シ人ナリ、索塞ノ小農ノ子ニシテ、幼年ノ時ニ、倫敦ノシテイ〔交易繁盛ノ市街〕ニ送ラレ、貨物棧房ノ小厮トナレリ、格伯田、勤敏ニシテ、ソノ行正ク又甚見聞ヲ廣ルヿヲ好ケリ、ソノ主人ハ、昔シ鄕校ニ在テ學ビタル人ナリシ故、格伯田ノ書ヲ讀ヿノ過度ナルヲ見テ、コレヲ戒メケルガ、コノ童子己ノ嗜好ニ任セ、書中ニ遇トコロノ寶貨ヲ、ソノ心ニ貯ルヿヲ勉タリ、コレヨリ次第ニ發運シ、後滿遞士打ニ住シ、白布ニ花ヲ印スルヿヲ業トセリ、格伯田常ニ公衆ノ疑問ニ心ヲ用ヒ、就中、民衆ノ敎育タルベキ事ニ意ヲ注キタリ、抑モ古ヨリ英國ニ於テ穀物入口ノ稅ヲ收ムルヿ、立テ法制トナリシガ、格伯田コノ法ノ公益ナラザルヿヲ熟知シ、コレヲ廢セント欲シテ、錢財ヲ費シ、心力ヲ竭シタリ、既ニシテ巴力門公議協同シテ、コノ法ヲ廢セシハ、實ニ格伯田ノ力ナリ、

ruby.r: パブリツクヱツシヨン
ボビユラアヱデユケイシヨン

blocks.genbun: Among like men of the same class may be ranked the late Richard Cobden, whose start in life was equally humble. The son of a small farmer at Midhurst in Sussex, he was sent at an early age to London and employed as a boy in a warehouse in the City. He was diligent, well conducted, and eager for information. His master, a man of the old school, warned him against too much reading; but the boy went on in his own course, storing his mind with the wealth found in books. He was promoted from one position of trust to another—became a traveller for his house—secured a large connection, and eventually started in business as a calico printer at Manchester. Taking an interest in public questions, more especially in popular education, his attention was gradually drawn to the subject of the Corn Laws, to the repeal of which he may be said to have devoted his fortune and his life.
